5cb102e8fe7ee437: BARCELONA: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick is hoping teenage star Lamine Yamal is fit to face Valencia in La Liga on Sunday after taking a knock.
The 19-year-old winger did not train with his team-mates on Saturday but instead worked by himself at the training ground.
"For tomorrow we have to wait, I cannot say it today," Flick told reporters Saturday.
"We have to decide if it's better that he rests or he starts from the beginning, I'll speak with him and we'll decide that.
"Lamine is a player who likes to play football."
Flick said Yamal will travel with the team to Mestalla stadium, where Barca are looking to continue their 100 percent start to the season.
"He trained separately and everything was good, he will travel with us tomorrow," said Flick.
"He took a hit and he had some pain so we said it's better that he trains separately," added the coach.
"After the training he said everything was good so he will travel and hopefully he can play tomorrow."
Yamal impressed in the 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday, netting his first two goals of the season.
Rivals Real Madrid slipped up in a 1-0 defeat at Real Betis on Friday, giving champions Barca the chance to establish themselves as sole league leaders.
"When you see the game yesterday, Real Madrid also played well... they had big, big chances," said Flick.
"This is football, (slipping up) can always happen. For us it's important that we focus on ourselves."
New arrival Gabriel Jesus is likely to begin on the bench with winger Raphinha staying as the starting striker after notching five goals in three games playing out of position.
"In this moment (Raphinha) is doing really great," explained Flick.
"He's the best option for us at the moment in this position."

3df50bd2ea408664: IPOH, Sept 5 — Police arrested two men yesterday over unlicensed money-lending and possession of ATM cards belonging to others, during an operation codenamed Ops Vulture in Teluk Intan.
Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said the suspects were arrested by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division.
He said the first arrest was at a Maybank ATM in Teluk Intan, involving a man who was making a cash withdrawal. Two ATM cards belonging to other people and RM300 cash were found on him.

“Following leads provided by the suspect, police then conducted a raid at a money-lending premises along Jalan Ah Cheong, Teluk Intan, which led to the arrest of a second man,” he said in a statement today.
He added that a search of the premises also uncovered three ATM cards and several pieces of gold jewellery, believed to be linked to the case. The seized items were estimated at RM2,050
He added that both suspects are being held at the Hilir Perak District Police Headquarters and they have been remanded until Sept 6 to assist in the investigation.
“The case is being investigated under Sections 420 and 424 of the Penal Code,” he said.
He advised the public against handing over their ATM cards or allowing others to use them, even when enticed with rewards.
“Members of the public are cautioned against engaging in any suspicious dealings involving the use of bank accounts or ATM cards, whether their own or belonging to others.

367d71ebd658b07f: BAGHDAD: Drivers formed long lines outside fuel stations in Baghdad on Saturday as gasoline supplies dropped in oil-rich Iraq due to import disruptions caused by the Middle East war.
Despite being OPEC's second largest oil producer, Iraq imports oil derivatives because its refineries do not produce enough gasoline to meet domestic demand.
In recent weeks, as regional hostilities drag on, long queues have been reappearing every few days, mostly outside government-run fuel stations in Baghdad and other provinces.
Baghdad resident Ibrahim Hashem waited for two hours outside a fuel station on Friday without any luck, only to return early the next day hoping to fill his car.
"It is unreasonable that we produce so many barrels of oil a day, yet still do not have enough gasoline to meet our daily needs," Hashem told AFP outside a fuel station in central Baghdad.
"We already suffer from traffic congestion because of the roads and lack of services. Now, it has become worse due to the gasoline shortage," he added.
Iraq's average daily consumption of gasoline is 33 million litres, but demand rises to 38 million when people panic over shortages, according to authorities.
The oil ministry said Friday that "regional events and the ongoing conflict are causing logistical challenges to tanker traffic, delaying their arrival at Iraqi ports."
It urged citizens to buy only the quantities they need and avoid crowding fuel stations for small amounts of gasoline.
Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said on Friday that his ministry was addressing the "temporary shortage of gasoline" and that new shipments will arrive soon to help stabilise supplies.
Like other oil producers, Iraq has been greatly affected by the US-Iran conflict, which has choked off the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
Iraq is hugely dependent on oil exports, which make up about 90 percent of its budget revenues.
Before the war erupted in February, Iraq produced around four million barrels per day, and exported an average of 3.4 million bpd, mostly via Hormuz.
After a significant drop, Iraqi oil exports recovered to more than 2.2 million bpd in August, according to the oil ministry.
Last month, Iran's state news agency IRNA said that over the past six months, Tehran has granted permission to "a number of Iraqi oil tankers" to pass through Hormuz.

5105475474d86b54: KUALA LUMPUR: Manchester United's enduring global appeal was on full display at the Malaysia Airlines Pavilion at the Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (MATTA) Fair 2026 today, with more than 500 fans turning up to meet club legends Park Ji-sung, Wes Brown and Edwin van der Sar.
The event not only drew supporters from across Malaysia but also fans who travelled from overseas, a testament to the English Premier League giants' worldwide following.

Among them was avid Red Devils memorabilia collector Adam Schwereb, 52, from Sydney, who flew into Malaysia to attend the event and meet the Manchester United legends, an opportunity he described as "too good to be missed'.

"I flew in last Wednesday to come to MATTA Fair. It's always a good opportunity, coming in from down south to catch up with the boys. And it's Manchester United; we travel the world for it," he told Bernama on the sidelines of the fair here.

Schwereb, who has attended matches at Old Trafford on several occasions, said events such as this provided supporters who could not travel to England with a rare opportunity to meet their footballing heroes in person.
The lifelong supporter said the initiative was particularly meaningful for younger fans who could now meet players who had played a key role in Manchester United's decorated history.
He also revealed that the trip would add two prized pieces to his personal Manchester United collection, with items from Park and Van der Sar becoming part of his museum in Sydney.
Young Vietnamese fan Nguyen Danh Truong, 12, was among the foreign fans at the event, travelling from Ho Chi Minh City to Malaysia with his father Nguyen Van Tai.
Truong, who is spending three days in Malaysia, said the meet-and-greet session was the sole reason his father planned the trip.

Meanwhile, Bryan Foong, chief executive officer of Airline Business at Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), the parent company of Malaysia Airlines, said the strong response from supporters reflected the strength of Manchester United's fan base globally and the value of the airline's partnership with the club.
"It's very popular. A lot of people come. It also helps us to create the business and the buzz around Malaysia Airlines as well," he said.

Foong said the airline's three-year partnership with Manchester United, which began in 2023, had so far been particularly effective in boosting the national carrier's visibility and market presence, given the club's extensive fan base across markets it served.
"The fan base for Manchester United is huge, right? And for us, they're important and spread out across the world.

"Wherever we are, in terms of where we fly to, like Australia, Southeast Asia, India and even to the United Kingdom, they're very well received and the Manchester United fans are very loyal. So it's a good partnership for us," he said.– BERNAMA
175a50ee348e6dfe: KOTA BHARU: PAS has played down speculation that Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s absence from its muktamar yesterday reflected a breakdown in Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional cooperation ahead of the Melaka election.

2050d46fc8cc5032: KULAI, Sept 5 — The government hopes Meta will expand its safety features for Facebook and Instagram users under the age of 18 worldwide as soon as possible, including daily usage limits and restrictions on access at night.

Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the safety features should not be limited to users in the United States, as young people in other countries, including Malaysia, also face the risk of internet addiction.
She said the measures are in line with the government’s direction to ensure that young people, particularly those under 16, do not use social media excessively.

“These measures are very important to ensure that internet addiction can be properly addressed, and we want to ensure that when everyone has access to the internet, young people also receive the protection they need,” she told reporters today after inspecting a damaged futsal court in Taman Desa Kulai.

Teo said this when commenting on the settlement of legal action involving Meta and 47 states, the District of Columbia and several US territories over allegations that Facebook and Instagram were designed with features that could cause addiction among children and teenagers.
Under the settlement, Meta has agreed to pay up to US$17.1 billion, in addition to making several changes to Facebook and Instagram to strengthen protections for underage users.
Teo said the changes include limiting the use of both platforms to two hours a day for users under 18, as well as restricting access between midnight and 6am.
Meta will also improve age verification and reduce several features that could encourage excessive use.
“Features such as ‘infinite scroll’ and ‘auto-feed’ will be discontinued, and Meta has also pledged to hide the number of ‘likes’ for underage users.
“This is to ensure that young people do not become overly focused on chasing ‘likes’ to the extent of doing something unwise simply to make their posts go viral,” she said.
She said social media platforms in Malaysia are still being given a grace period to implement measures related to restricting usage among underage users.
“Some people have asked me why their children aged 16 and below can still use social media. This is because the platforms requested a grace period, and we are still within that period,” she said.
Teo said measures to protect young people must be implemented comprehensively by all social media platforms and not just Meta.
She said restrictions on Facebook and Instagram alone would not be sufficient if other platforms such as TikTok, YouTube and Snapchat did not take similar measures.
“I think this is the right time for all social media platforms to give this serious consideration and ensure that their platforms are safe for young people.
“These measures are very important to ensure that internet addiction can be properly addressed and that young people receive the protection they need,” she said. — Bernama

457b0bad8c0e022e: MANILA: Philippine vice president Sara Duterte posted bail at a Manila courthouse on Saturday, a day after an arrest warrant was issued over her alleged death threat against the country's president.

Duterte was charged last month with "grave threats" stemming from a late-night news briefing in which she claimed to have hired a hitman to kill President Ferdinand Marcos, his wife and a congressman cousin should she be cut down first.
She later said the comments had been misconstrued.
The alleged assassination threat also forms a crucial element of her ongoing Senate impeachment trial, where a guilty verdict would see her removed from office and permanently banned from politics.
"The vice president voluntarily appeared before the court that issued the warrant, so there was no need for her to be arrested," her lawyer Lawrence Lim said.
He was speaking after Duterte emerged from the courthouse holding a court order confirming she had posted a cash bond totalling 360,000 pesos ($5,740).
She also underwent a standard booking procedure in which her fingerprints were recorded, though no mugshots were taken, Lim said.
Duterte said in a statement that her lawyers advised her to post bail for her safety.

"They explained to me that I would have better protection from civilians who would be able to monitor my situation, rather than being in detention where I would be isolated and have little protection," she said.
Prior to entering the courthouse, Duterte told reporters she feared for her life.
"I don't want to (post bail) if no one is watching," she said, claiming to be the victim of police harassment.
"Will they throw me into the (jail) and then one night I die in my sleep?" she said.
'GRAVE THREATS'
The Philippine presidential palace rejected Duterte's comments as "unfounded", saying police were merely implementing their mandate to protect Filipinos.
"This administration will never allow the police to be used to commit any form of violence," it said.
Under the Philippine legal code, a criminal conviction on the "grave threats" charge could carry a jail term of up to six months.
The vice president's legal team issued a statement on Friday saying she had "no intention of evading the law and will continue to exercise all her legal remedies."
Justice department officials have rejected her lawyers' argument that the vice president cannot be prosecuted for offences that are also tied to her impeachment.
Duterte was impeached in May by the House of Representatives, the lower chamber of parliament, on charges that also included graft and corruption.
A guilty verdict in the Senate – where her trial recently concluded its ninth week – would spell an end to a planned run for president in 2028.
Duterte first announced her candidacy in February.

d9a7eae05bc15065: JUBA: A deadly attack on a military base in South Sudan, combined with the declaration of an "unprecedented" drought emergency, have underlined the challenges facing the world's youngest nation as it prepares for its first elections.
South Sudan in eastern Africa is among the poorest and most corrupt countries on the planet but is attempting to hold elections in December for the first time since gaining independence in 2011.

On Friday, a group of armed men attacked the military base in Warrap, in the country's northeast, killing 16 military and police personnel, and four civilians, state information minister William Deng Wol told AFP.
Also on Friday, the state declared an emergency over a prolonged drought.

"The state faces an unprecedented dry spell caused by severe rainfall deficits, causing severe crop failures, also leading to catastrophic loss of livestock and grazing lands," the information minister said in a statement.

With the El Nino weather pattern threatening much of eastern Africa with major climate disasters in the coming weeks, the Warrap official appealed for help from the central government and international partners "to avert the looming catastrophic famine".

Warrap State is plagued by inter-communal violence, usually involving revenge killings and cattle raids, though it was not clear what triggered the attack on the military base, which also led to the deaths of six attackers.
The country faces myriad challenges at a time when international aid is also falling sharply.
South Sudan's government under president Salva Kiir is considered one of the most corrupt in the world.
A UN report last year detailed how officials had stolen billions of dollars in oil money while leaving the population with hardly any essential services.
Shortly after independence, the country was plunged into a devastating civil war between Kiir and his longtime rival, Riek Machar.
A 2018 power-sharing agreement brought peace but has lately fallen apart, with Machar now under arrest and facing a treason trial. Their forces have fought sporadic battles in recent months.

In these circumstances, the long-awaited elections could fuel renewed conflict and heighten the risk of atrocities, the UN-appointed Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan said last month. It is due to hold another fact-finding mission this week.
60b3e975f99e54fe: NUWAKOT (Nepal), Sept 5 — Rescuers pulled a Nepali woman alive today from her home buried under thick mud and debris when the region was struck by massive flooding 10 days ago.
Emergency personnel said earlier they had rescued a Chinese man found alive inside a tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal’s Rasuwa district.
Members of Nepal’s Armed Police Force cheered as the mud-caked 64-year-old woman, Chandrika Shrestha, was pulled from her buried home in Nuwakot district.
“A police team found her as they were clearing the area. She has been airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment,” police deputy superintendent Iqbal Hawari told AFP.

This handout photograph taken and released on September 5, 2026 by Nepal Army shows security personnel assisting a woman rescued from a flash-flood ravaged house at Betrawati in Nepal's Nuwakot district. Devastating floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 1,287 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said September 4, with the number of missing at 5,083. — Nepal Army handout via AFP pic
A video released by Nepal’s Armed Police Force showed only a part of her house visible, with the lower floors completely submerged by thick sludge.

Emergency response teams have been working relentlessly to find survivors since a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a glacial and rock collapse on August 26.
So far, 1,344 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the national disaster agency, with about 5,000 people missing.
In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing.
That takes the overall death toll to 1,375 people, with more than 5,500 missing. — AFP
4f53bdf2e5af73ba: PETALING JAYA: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah has called for greater emphasis on early cancer detection, stressing that access to health screening should be available to all Malaysians regardless of their social or economic background.

In his address at the launch of the National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026 today, the ruler said a national screening programme should reach everyone, describing it as an important investment in the nation's wellbeing.

"Hope must also live in early detection more broadly. A national screening programme that reaches a plantation worker as easily as a company executive is not a luxury but one of the best investments we can make in the wellbeing of our people.
"I hope our health authorities, our insurers, our employers and every Malaysian family will come to see screening as an act of love, for ourselves and for those who depend on us."
On the congress, Sultan Nazrin outlined three priorities, calling for stronger research, evidence-based policymaking and greater public awareness of cancer.
"First, that our scientists and doctors continue research that is useful as well as rigorous, reaching patients in every state, not only our biggest cities.
"Second, that our policymakers listen closely to the evidence and the personal stories shared here and carry them into our national cancer strategy.
"Third, that each of us remembers that fighting cancer begins with our own choices, our own workplaces, and our willingness to talk openly about a disease too often discussed in hushed whispers."
Sultan Nazrin said no single hospital, ministry, university or congress could defeat cancer alone, stressing that progress required collective action.
He cited the partnership between the National Cancer Society of Malaysia and Sunway University as an example of the collaboration Malaysia needed to move the fight against cancer forward.
"There was a time when a cancer diagnosis was spoken of only in whispers, almost a final sentence rather than something that could be faced, and overcome.

"I am glad to say this is changing. Survival rates for many cancers have improved enormously within a single generation and Malaysian researchers and institutions are contributing real, original science to this progress, not simply borrowing it from elsewhere."

Also present were Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah, National Cancer Society Malaysia president Datuk Dr Saunthari Somasundaram and Health Ministry deputy director-general (public health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.

6ac9db0a68f1953f: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 5 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek will propose including the Kasih Madani home childminder training programme in Budget 2027 to provide greater childcare and safety support for working mothers.

Fadhlina, who is also the Nibong Tebal MP, said expanding the initiative would allow more childminders to receive formal training, improve childcare quality, and strengthen the home childcare ecosystem.
She said the cause was close to her heart as a mother of six who faced immense challenges securing reliable childcare while working as a lawyer.
Sharing her personal experience, Fadhlina revealed that three of her children were cared for by home childminders, and her second child was subjected to physical abuse by a childminder.

“My second child was abused by a childminder who caned the child’s legs. At the time, I felt overwhelming guilt because as a working mother and lawyer with a demanding schedule, I had no choice but to rely on a childminder,” she said.

“That experience made me realise that childminders must possess both commitment and a sense of responsibility to society,” she said after officiating the Gala Pesona Kasih Madani at the PICCA@Arena Butterworth Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Merdeka Center programme director Ibrahim Suffian and Yayasan Sime Darby chief executive officer Dr Yatela Zainal Abidin.

Elaborating, Fadhlina shared another personal tragedy, namely the loss of her fourth child to Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), which left her torn between pursuing her career and staying home to care for her children.
However, she said strong support from her extended family, including her siblings, helped ensure her children received proper care while she worked.
She stressed that child protection must not end at the childminding stage, but should extend seamlessly into formal schooling through a comprehensive policy framework.

“That is why at the Ministry of Education level, we are continuing with the Child Protection Policy in schools. Everyone shares a responsibility for child protection, from home childcare all the way to school,” she said.
Fadhlina added that granting formal recognition to childminders through Kasih Madani training was a vital step in elevating the dignity of the profession.
She said certified childminders should take pride in their work, as their role directly enabled working women to remain in the workforce and contribute to national development.
More than 1,000 childminders across four states, namely Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah, and Penang, have benefited from the Kasih Madani initiative since its launch in August last year.

Managed by the Merdeka Center with support from the Ministry of Finance through Yayasan Sime Darby, Kasih Madani aligns with the Madani Government’s vision to strengthen Malaysia’s childcare ecosystem through the empowerment of home and community childminders.

The initiative equips childminders with essential skills and knowledge through courses such as the Madani Childcare Pilot Course (Karisma), the Madani Childcare Seminar (Semai), professionalisation workshops, and community outreach programmes. — Bernama
17b8d827485f8d5e: KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Safety Expert Association (RSEA) has called for an immediate structural safety audit of potentially hazardous structures along Malaysia's major expressways following the collapse of a large structure onto the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) near Shah Alam last night.

RSEA founder and road safety and motorsports adviser Jamil Manan Supri said the incident raised a critical road safety issue, stressing that structures located beside or above high-speed traffic must remain structurally sound throughout their service life.

"A structural failure on an expressway is not simply an infrastructure or traffic management problem. It has the potential to become a mass-casualty road safety hazard, particularly when motorists travelling at high speed have only seconds to detect and respond to an unexpected obstruction.

"RSEA therefore calls for an immediate structural safety audit of all large billboards, advertising structures, gantries and other potentially hazardous structures located along major expressways, with priority given to those positioned above, immediately beside or within the potential fall zone of live traffic," he said in a statement.

Jamil said the inspection must go beyond visual checks and include assessments of foundations, anchoring systems, bolts, welds and supporting frames, as well as corrosion, structural fatigue, deformation, vibration and wind-loading capacity.

"Every structure should be subject to mandatory periodic inspection and certification by competent and appropriately qualified professionals, with additional inspections following severe weather, vehicle impact or other abnormal events," he said.
He said the location of billboards must also be assessed from a road-user safety perspective, rather than solely for commercial visibility.

"Before a billboard or large advertising structure is approved, authorities should assess its potential fall zone and determine whether its failure could block multiple lanes, obstruct sight distance, interfere with traffic signs or create a serious hazard to motorists, particularly vulnerable road users such as motorcyclists.
"At the same time, the increasing use of illuminated and digital billboards requires stronger controls. Billboard lighting must not become a source of driver distraction or glare.

"Brightness, flashing, animation, rapid image changes, colour contrast, operating hours and positioning within the driver's field of vision should be regulated to ensure that advertising does not compete with traffic signs, signals, emergency warnings or other critical road information."

Jamil said RSEA also proposed the establishment of a National Highway Advertising and Structural Safety Register, clearly identifying the owner, designer, installer, approval status, structural certification, inspection history, maintenance records and next inspection date for every high-risk structure.

"This incident should therefore serve as a warning to all relevant authorities, highway operators, billboard owners and advertisers. Safety cannot be treated as a one-time approval requirement. It must be continuously managed throughout the entire lifecycle of the structure," he said.
Last night, all northbound lanes of the NKVE near Shah Alam were blocked, bringing traffic to a standstill shortly before midnight.
Photographs and video from the scene showed what appeared to be a large overhead highway gantry lying across the carriageway, with several heavy vehicles, including lorries, nearby.
71ce42f1a07885cf: PETALING JAYA: Ahli Parlimen DAP Ramkarpal Singh membidas seorang Adun PAS dari Kedah susulan dakwaan partinya hipokrit kerana menyeru peguam negara menyemak semula keputusan menghentikan 47 pertuduhan dihadapi Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi.

Semalam, Adun Pengkalan Kundor Mardhiyyah Johari, berkata isu berkenaan tidak dibangkitkan sewaktu DAP dan sekutunya dalam Pakatan Harapan (PH) memerlukan sokongan Umno untuk membentuk kerajaan persekutuan selepas PRU 2022.
Ramkarpal, yang juga Ahli Parlimen Bukit Gelugor, berkata kenyataan Mardhiyyah "jelas tidak tepat dan menunjukkan beliau tidak memahami pendirian DAP" berkait kes Zahid.

Beliau berkata, sekiranya Adun tersebut menyemak fakta, jelas DAP membangkitkan kebimbangan serius mengenai isu itu sejurus selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan Zahid dilepas tanpa dibebaskan (DNAA) pada 4 Sept 2023, berikutan permohonan pihak pendakwaan.
Beliau menekankan bahawa Setiausaha Agung DAP Loke Siew Fook telah mengeluarkan kenyataan pada keesokan hari, bagi menuntut peguam negara memberi penjelasan mengenai keputusan dibuat.

"Loke ketika itu turut menegaskan DAP sentiasa mempertahankan prinsip pengasingan kuasa antara cabang kehakiman, eksekutif dan legislatif serta memastikan tiada campur tangan eksekutif dalam mana-mana kes di mahkamah, sambil menegaskan perkara tersebut adalah di dalam kepentingan awam," katanya.

Ramkarpal sebagai pengerusi Biro Undang-undang DAP, berkata parti itu juga menuntut Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) menjelaskan sebab memutuskan tidak meneruskan tindakan lanjut terhadap Zahid, seperti dinyatakan dalam kenyataan, pada 7 Jan lalu.

Beliau berkata, pada 8 Jan lalu, beliau juga mempersoal tindakan AGC secara tiba-tiba berpendirian dapatan prima facie Mahkamah Tinggi terhadap Zahid tidak lagi kukuh, sedangkan dapatan tersebut dibuat berdasarkan bukti yang dikemukakan sendiri pihak pendakwaan.

Sambil menegaskan apa disuarakan DAP berkait DNAA Zahid bukan sesuatu yang baru, Ramkarpal berkata, DAP akan terus mempersoalkan keputusan peguam negara dalam kes Zahid kerana keputusan berkenaan jelas tidak masuk akal, khususnya apabila Mahkamah Tinggi membuat dapatan prima facie terhadap Zahid.

"Persoalan yang sepatutnya timbul sekarang ialah sama ada PAS akan melakukan perkara yang sama atau memilih berdiam diri, lebih-lebih lagi ketika Umno dan PAS dilihat semakin mempunyai hubungan yang begitu akrab pada masa ini," katanya.
Pada Khamis, Ahli Parlimen Jelutong RSN Rayer menggesa peguam negara menyemak semula kes Zahid, disusuli Pemuda DAP menyokong seruan tersebut pada Jumaat.
Zahid, yang juga timbalan perdana menteri, diberikan DNAA atas 47 pertuduhan melibatkan rasuah, pengubahan wang haram, dan pecah amanah dalam kes Yayasan Akalbudi.
Kes tersebut telah mencapai peringkat pembelaan, dengan Zahid dan 14 saksi pembelaan lain telah memberi keterangan apabila pihak pendakwaan memohon pelepasan bersyarat.
d3cc71180b3e137a: KUALA LUMPUR: Six areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm, with the state remaining the worst affected by the haze.
Data published on the Department of Environment's Facebook page showed that 25 of 68 monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, while another six recorded very unhealthy readings.
Kuching recorded the country's highest API reading at 275, followed by Sri Aman at 235, Serian at 230, Samarahan at 210, Bintulu at 209 and Samalaju at 208.
Under the API classification, readings above 200 are categorised as very unhealthy.
Stations recording unhealthy air quality included ILP Miri (191), Mukah (190), Miri (184), Sarikei (180), Sibu (176), Kimanis (171) and Labuan (170).

Other locations reporting unhealthy air quality included Limbang (163), Johan Setia (161), Bukit Rambai (159), Tangkak (158), Kota Kinabalu (158), Kluang (156), Nilai and Segamat (157 each), Seremban and Alor Gajah (155 each), as well as Putrajaya (151).
The data also showed that 26 stations recorded moderate air quality, while 10 recorded good air quality. No station recorded a hazardous API reading.
The API measures air quality based on pollutants including particulate matter. Readings from 101 to 200 are classified as unhealthy, while those exceeding 200 are categorised as very unhealthy.
The distribution map showed poorer air quality concentrated mainly in parts of Sarawak, while several areas in Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah also recorded unhealthy readings.
1e4e7afbe0b08d85: PARIS: Fenerbahce duo Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi have been suspended for their part in the chaotic scenes after their club's Champions League play-off second leg against Lyon.

Last month's 2-1 victory for Fenerbahce in France meant the Turks progressed 3-2 on aggregate and after the final whistle, Greenwood and Guendouzi, who both previously played for Lyon's bitter rivals Marseille, were involved in a brawl with players and coaching staff from both sides.

Former Arsenal midfielder Guendouzi has been suspended "for a total of four Uefa club competition matches for which he would otherwise be eligible, for insulting others present at the match, provoking spectators and for violating the basic rules of decent conduct," Uefa announced in a decision made public on Friday evening.
Two of the matches are subject to a "one-year probationary period", European football's governing body added in the statement.
Guendouzi, who was also fined €50,000 (US$58,000), was found guilty, among other things, of giving the middle finger to Lyon supporters and of provocations that led to a scuffle after the match.
His English teammate Mason Greenwood, formerly of Manchester United, received a one-match suspended ban and was fined €30,000 for "violating the basic rules of decent conduct".
ad313b76a687a701: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Serian remains under the haze emergency despite its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading improving from the hazardous level, with the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) continuing to closely monitor the situation.

SDMC chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said in a statement today that the Serian air quality monitoring station recorded an API reading of 334 as at 10am, placing the area in the hazardous category.
However, the reading fell to 273 by 2pm, bringing it into the very unhealthy category.
He said SDMC would monitor the API reading over the next three days to observe any fluctuations, particularly the possibility of it rising above 500.
“The API is primarily affected by the wind direction and source of hotspots,” he said.
Uggah said the monitoring would be carried out before any recommendation was made to the Sarawak Premier and Prime Minister regarding the status of the emergency in Serian.

Yesterday, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consented to the declaration of an emergency in the Serian Division following worsening haze that had pushed air pollution to hazardous levels, with API readings exceeding 500.

The Prime Minister’s Office, in a statement yesterday, said the decision was made after taking into consideration the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and relevant agencies monitoring air quality in the affected area.
Although Serian remains under the emergency, Uggah said government and private offices, as well as other workplaces in the affected area, may continue operating.
This includes industries, plantations, construction sites and quarries.
“However, they must take health precautionary measures,” he said.
Uggah said SDMC was also closely monitoring air quality, weather conditions, hotspots and haze movement across Sarawak so that appropriate action could be taken as the situation develops.
The public was advised to avoid outdoor activities, while those who could not avoid exposure outdoors were advised to wear an N95 mask or, at minimum, a three-ply mask.
Uggah also urged the public to take particular care of children, senior citizens and other vulnerable groups who may be more affected by the haze.
He said SDMC would continue to monitor the situation closely and issue further updates as necessary.
The committee would also continue working closely with relevant State and Federal agencies to manage the situation.
“The health, safety and wellbeing of the people of Sarawak remain our highest priority,” he said. — The Borneo Post
36557bbeaf4416b2: GEORGE TOWN: Former Singapore diplomat Kishore Mahbubani has warned that a potential armed conflict between China and Taiwan could pose a serious threat to Southeast Asia, cautioning the region against assuming it would remain unaffected.
Kishore, also a former president of the United Nations Security Council, warned that if a war occurred between the two countries, the chances of US involvement would be very high.
"And I think if we in Southeast Asia naively believe that a war across Taiwan will have no impact on us, then I would say that we are really living in a fool's paradise.

"We have to be aware that a war between China and Taiwan will have incredibly negative consequences for, in fact, the whole world and also for our region," he said in a fireside chat session held during the Penang Peace Dialogue conference at a hotel here today.
Later, Kishore told FMT that Southeast Asia would suffer from US involvement in a China-Taiwan war because the global economy would take a hit from the conflict.
"Global economic growth will go down, and our economies will suffer. There are many ways we'll suffer. So, that is why we should prevent it," he said.
Taiwan's independence move could spark conflict

Kishore said that in order for the international community to prevent a Sino-Taiwan war from taking place, it should not support the conditions that will start such a war - which is Taiwan's move to declare independence.
"If Taiwan declares independence, China will declare war on Taiwan, and then we will go down a slippery slope towards a global conflict," he said.
He also shared that he told the Taiwanese that many have died fighting proxy wars since World War II, citing the Russia-Ukraine war as an example.
For Taiwan not to suffer a fate similar to Ukraine's, he said, it should understand the red lines and ensure it does not cross them.
However, Kishore also said this does not mean the destiny of the Taiwanese is simply to be subjected by China.

"It is conceivable to work out all kinds of arrangements whereby the people of Taiwan enjoy autonomy, a good life, and have exactly what they have today, but yet, in principle, they are reunified with China.
"There are many creative diplomatic ways to find a solution, and you can look for those creative diplomatic ways to avoid any kind of war that would damage all of us," he said.
Last month, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim came under scrutiny over his remarks in an Al Jazeera interview, where he said he sees Taiwan as part of China.
Anwar's statement drew praise from Beijing but condemnation from Taiwan, which warned that his “one-sided support” for China could affect the confidence of Taiwanese businesses investing in Malaysia.
Anwar stood by his remarks, saying that Malaysia's one-China policy dates back to the era of then prime minister Abdul Razak Hussein and remains unchanged.
He also said Malaysia respects China's position on Taiwan and believes a peaceful approach is the best way forward.
China has long claimed that democratically governed Taiwan is its territory and maintains that any formal move towards independence will trigger a military response.
ed09dac2eb780f9c: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department will intensify enforcement operations to track down foreigners holding more than 1,300 Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) believed to have been irregularly approved through a syndicate uncovered under Op Crack.

Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department's enforcement division was also gathering intelligence on the ground to identify and locate foreigners holding the improperly approved passes.
"We will continue carrying out enforcement operations to trace the holders of PLKS that were approved irregularly.
"There are at least 1,300 of these PLKS which are believed to be in the hands of foreigners after being issued through the syndicate.
"We will either catch them through intelligence gathered or through targeted operations," he told the New Straits Times.
Zakaria said the department also welcomed information from the public that could assist enforcement officers in locating foreigners holding the irregularly approved PLKS.
He said information received would help the department identify and track down those who had benefited from the syndicate's activities.
"Rest assured that the identities of those who come forward with information would be kept strictly confidential," he said.
It was previously reported that immigration officers attempting to track down holders of the irregularly issued PLKS hit a snag after finding that their registered addresses were also fake.
The department conducted several raids at addresses linked to the affected permits as part of ongoing investigations.
However, officers found that the information registered under the permits did not correspond with the actual locations.
Zakaria said then that although their system contained certain addresses, officers found different premises when they visited the locations, while the employer information also did not match.

The department had earlier said it would cancel all improperly approved PLKS and trace their holders following the dismantling of a syndicate suspected of hacking the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to manipulate the pass approval process.

Zakaria had said the move was the first step following the discovery of PLKS approvals that did not comply with procedures during Op Crack, a joint operation between the Immigration Department and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
It was previously reported that 12 individuals, including six Immigration Department personnel and a police officer, were detained by the MACC for allegedly being involved in the syndicate.
Investigations found that 1,306 PLKS were allegedly approved through unused foreign-worker quotas, resulting in an estimated RM2.4 million in lost levy payments.
Nine bank accounts containing about RM300,000 were also reportedly frozen as part of the investigation.
b4ab849d48297b03: JAKARTA: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by encroaching wildfires to their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday.

The vast Southeast Asian archipelago has for weeks been fighting wildfires blanketing parts of Borneo and Sumatra with smog, with haze also contributing to air pollution in Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
The orangutan pair had been under observation since July after being spotted in a plantation area near a forest in West Kalimantan, a local natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.
But authorities decided to evacuate them to a rescue center managed by the wildlife foundation Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) on Thursday as fire spread near their habitat.
Their health is being closely monitored by veterinarians, but a preliminary check found no burn injuries on the two great apes.

"Exposure to smoke over a period of time... can affect the orangutan's respiratory system, especially when smoke concentrations in the habitat are very high," YIARI's veterinarian Komara, who like many Indonesians uses only one name, said in a statement.
"Both individuals will continue to be monitored while they are at the rescue and rehabilitation center."

The latest rescue means nine orangutans have been evacuated because of threats from wildfires in less than a month in the Ketapang district of West Kalimantan province, YIARI operational director Argitoe Ranting said.
"This shows that fires not only destroy forests but also deprive animals of shelter and food," Argitoe said.
Most animals "do not have many options" to relocate as their habitat burns, he added.

One orangutan died after being rescued last week, with a necropsy result pointing to smoke exposure as the cause of death, the West Kalimantan natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.

811b0d9c7fb52cc3: "THE struggle behind the collapse and rebuilding of community – which is the foundation of daily life – resonates with people today surrounded by uncertainty, while also delivering a gust of positivity," says director Lee Sang-Il.
He is referring to his 2006 film, 'Hula Girls', screened in a 4K remastered version as part of the Japanese Film Festival line-up for this year under the Japan Foundation.
Set in a declining Japanese mining town, 'Hula Girl's follows a group of young women who learn the Hawaiian hula to help revitalise their community.
It won several awards, including the Japanese Academy's Best Film award in 2007.
The 52-year-old says audiences might also find 'Hula Girls' interesting after all these years due to the popularity of his most recent film, 'Kokuho'.
The latter, which won the Japanese Academy's 2026 Best Film and Best Director awards, is about a gangster family-born boy who finds himself adopted by a kabuki actor.
'Kokuho', Japan's 2026 Oscar submission, will have a special screening on Sept 9 at GSC MidValley and GSC MyTown in Kuala Lumpur.
"Although there is a difference in degree, perhaps many audiences find meaning in the shared theme of unwavering focus of a person dedicating their life to art," says Lee.
Having also won awards for his screenplays, Lee says he has never considered releasing books to go with his movies.

"I'm conscious of the fact that my sensibilities are best suited for converting written word into images. For example, a long verbal exchange in a novel might be conveyed without a word being said, just by the atmosphere between the actors or some imagery. And conversely, the invisible emotions buried between lines of text could be given shape by an image.
"It's because I firmly believe my abilities can be best used to show through interpretation a different facet of a character, or unearthing a lode buried within the story."
The acclaimed film director says he gets a sense of fulfilment from filmmaking.

"There was nothing else that I liked. Meaning, I like films. If I were shooting a film, one naturally feels it upon completion, but there's an additional sense of achievement when it reaches an audience, and sometimes it may reach viewers overseas, like this time. The high I get is difficult to get elsewhere."

Lee's 'Hula Girls' is part of JFF's Girl Power selection, movies inspired by real-life events. The other two films in this section are ''Fujiko' and 'Purehearted'. 'Fujiko', a 2026 movie, was screened at the JFF press conference in mid-August.

It is about a young woman who fights to get her daughter back and raises her as a single mother. Interestingly, director Taichi Kimura has incorporated J-rock and psychedelic rock into the film score.

JFF pays tribute to Yamada Yoji, celebrating 65 years of his contribution to cinema. The 95-year-old filmmaker will have four of his films featured – 'Tokyo Taxi', 'A Distant Cry from Spring', Tora-san's 'Many Splintered Love' and 'Renjishi' (The Father and Son Shishi Lions).

Another highlight is Akira Kurosawa's classic 'Throne of Blood' (1957), an adaptation of Shakespeare's 'Macbeth', which remains one of the most acclaimed Japanese interpretations of the classic tragedy.
The festival this year presents a total of 15 films. They include the anime 'Chimney Town: Frozen in Time', 'One Last Love Letter', and 'Samurai Vengeance'.
The festival runs Sept 8 to Oct 18, travelling to GSC cinemas in five states, including Klang Valley, Penang (Sept 17-20), Johor Baru (Sept 24-27), Kuching (Oct 8-11) and Kota Kinabalu (Oct 15-18).
Visit GSC or Japan Foundation websites for more details.

b223dd714593dd3a: KUALA LUMPUR: Chemical emissions from industries, vehicle exhaust fumes, as well as water and soil pollution can no longer be regarded solely as environmental issues, as prolonged exposure has been linked to various cancers, including among children.

Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said cancer prevention efforts should not focus solely on factors such as smoking and diet, but also address chemicals released by factories, vehicle emissions and other pollutants children may inhale or be exposed to daily.
He said the issue represented a gap that was not discussed often enough, despite the potential harm caused by environmental exposure.
"It sits in the shadows behind many of the cancer cases that fill our hospitals: the air our children breathe and the harm that too often is caused by what is hidden within it."
Sultan Nazrin said this at the launch of the National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026 and the coffee table book, A Breath For The Future: Malaysia's National Lung Health Initiative.

He said the concern was particularly pertinent given the difficult environmental conditions affecting the region, including forest fires in Kalimantan, a dry season intensified by El Nino and winds blowing in an unfavourable direction for Malaysia.
He also urged Malaysia to take note of the emergence of so-called "cancer alleys", where heavy industry had grown faster than safeguards intended to protect nearby communities.

Citing communities in Louisiana in the United States, industrial areas in South Africa and China, and the Niger Delta in West Africa, where concerns had emerged over cancer risks associated with industrial activity and pollution, he said Malaysia should regard such examples as a warning.

"This is not a problem unique to any one country or industry and it is a pattern we in Malaysia, with our own industrial corridors and our own rivers running past factories and plantations, would be wise to take as a caution rather than a distant headline."

Sultan Nazrin also highlighted a documentary about a community in southern Iraq living near intensive oil and gas extraction, where routine gas flaring exposed residents to potentially harmful chemicals and children reportedly experienced unusually high rates of leukaemia.
He said the example illustrated the broader health risks posed by pollution, noting that scientists had learned over many years that pollution did not only harm the lungs.

"Chemicals released by industry, by traffic and by the fuels we burn to run both have been linked to childhood leukaemia and to cancers of the lung, the bladder and the breast in adults exposed over many years.
"Polluted water and soil bring their own dangers too, linked to cancers of the liver and digestive system downstream of poorly regulated factories.
"So when we talk about preventing cancer, we cannot speak only of smoking and diet, important as those are.
"We must also speak honestly about what our factories release, what our vehicles put into our streets and what we allow to settle into the lungs of a sleeping child."
Sultan Nazrin said Malaysia must therefore consider how it balances economic growth with environmental safeguards.
Pointing to London as an example, he said stronger environmental regulation could produce measurable improvements in public health.
Following the introduction of its Ultra Low Emission Zone, which charges the most polluting vehicles high fees to enter the city centre, children in central London
experienced significant improvements in lung function as toxic vehicle emissions fell.
"Before the scheme began, children in central London had noticeably weaker lungs than children in Luton, a town near London.
"Within five years, as toxic exhaust fell sharply in London, those children's lungs recovered so well that they nearly caught up with children in Luton.
"The number of London children with poorly functioning lungs fell from about one in seven to about one in 11.
"Damage many once thought was simply the price of city life turned out not to be permanent.
"Clean the air, and children's bodies can heal."
Sultan Nazrin said the lesson from London was a hopeful one.
"Pollution and disease are not simply facts of modern life we must accept. They are the result of choices, and choices can be changed.

"If a city as large as London can restore its children's lungs within five years, then Malaysia, blessed with rainforest, coastline and industries still young enough to build cleanly from the start, can protect the lungs and the futures of our own children."
He said addressing the issue was not a task for the Health Ministry alone, but required action across the environmental, transport and industrial sectors.

"It belongs equally to those responsible for our environment, our transport, our industry and business leaders, who must help weigh the cost of cleaner production against a cost that cannot be priced: a child's life.

"I say this not to single out any one sector, but because I believe Malaysia's industries, given the chance to lead on this, will find that cleaner growth and competitive growth need not be different things."

Present were Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah, National Cancer Society Malaysia president Datuk Dr Saunthari Somasundaram and Health Ministry deputy director-general (public health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.

1fb27e4ffeade16d: DHAKA: Thousands of opposition supporters launched a long march across Bangladesh on Saturday, piling pressure on prime minister Tarique Rahman's government over acute shortages of cooking gas, electricity, and fertiliser.
The action marks the first major street mobilisation against the government, which came to power in the South Asian country of 170 million people six months ago.
Waving banners and chanting slogans, crowds gathered at a public square in Dhaka before setting off on the first leg of a march to the port city of Chittagong, with rallies planned along the route.
"This movement is aimed at ensuring cooking gas and lighting up every household with electricity," opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman told supporters.
Bangladesh has been reeling from acute shortages, partly caused by the war in the Middle East, while questions have been raised over the government’s handling of the crisis.

The rally comes a day after the arrest of a college student who allegedly insulted senior government officials while venting frustration over high electricity bills, a move critics said reflected growing intolerance of dissent.
"You have failed to supply gas, electricity, and fertiliser and are not allowing people to even speak up," Akhter Hossen of the opposition National Citizen Party told the crowd.
af62504f185dbdca: PETALING JAYA: DAP MP Ramkarpal Singh has hit out at a PAS assemblyman from Kedah for questioning the timing of DAP urging the attorney-general to review the 47 charges faced by Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

Pengkalan Kundor assemblyman Mardhiyyah Johari said yesterday the issue was not raised when DAP and its allies in Pakatan Harapan needed Umno’s support to form the federal government after the 2022 general election.
Ramkarpal, who is the Bukit Gelugor MP, said Mardhiyyah “is clearly erroneous and ignorant of DAP’s stand on the matter”.

He said that if she had checked the facts, it would have become clear that DAP had raised serious concerns over the matter immediately after the High Court granted Zahid a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on Sept 4, 2023, following the prosecution's application.
He pointed out that DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook issued a statement the very next day, calling for the attorney-general to explain his decision.

“Loke had then said that DAP will always uphold the principle of separation of powers between judicial, executive and legislative branches and ensure there is no executive intervention in any court case, before pointing out that the issue was of public interest,” he said.

Ramkarpal, who is DAP’s legal bureau chairman, said the party had also urged the Attorney-General's Chambers to explain why it had decided to take no further action against Zahid, as stated in its statement dated Jan 7 this year.

He also said that on Jan 8, he asked the AGC why it had suddenly taken the view that the High Court’s prima facie findings against Zahid did not carry weight, particularly when those findings were based on evidence presented in court by the prosecution itself.

Ramkarpal said the party will continue asking questions about the attorney-general's decision in Zahid’s case “as it clearly makes no sense”, especially since the High Court had made prima facie findings against him.
“The question that arises instead is whether PAS will do the same or refrain from doing so, now that Umno and PAS seem to enjoy a cosy relationship with each other,” he said.
On Thursday, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer urged the attorney-general to review Zahid's case, with DAP Youth backing the call the following day.
Zahid, who is also the deputy prime minister, was granted a DNAA on 47 charges involving corruption, money laundering and criminal breach of trust in the Yayasan Akalbudi case.
The case had reached the defence stage, with Zahid and 14 other defence witnesses having testified when the prosecution applied for a conditional discharge.
7d33c98984c7b862: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Kong delivered a dramatic Group A Super Over win against Malaysia in the ACC Premier Cup at the UKM Oval in Bangi on Saturday.
After Hong Kong were bowled out for 209 runs in 46.3 overs, Malaysia reached 209-9 in 50 overs with Virandeep Singh hitting an unbeaten 82.
Hong Kong needed just three balls in the extra over as Anshuman Rath scored 12 runs with a six and two boundaries after Malaysia reached 11-1 with Virandeep netting a six.
Syahadat Ramli made 50 off 87 balls with a single but was then bowled by Hassan Khan off the next ball he faced.
Virandeep reached his 50 off 59 balls with a single, just after captain Syed Aziz Syed Mubarak (1) fell lbw to Ehsan Khan.
Syed Aziz's exit in the 34th over led to a struggle for Malaysia to score runs until Virandeep needed two runs off the last ball to force a Super Over.
This match was effectively a semi-final decider after Malaysia lost to Nepal on Thursday, with only Bahrain to come on Monday after beating Saudi Arabia in the opening match.
Nepal lead Group A with four points, level with Hong Kong, who have played a match more.

"We would have loved to have won the game, and Virandeep and Syahadat were brilliant again, but it was a hard wicket. The result went the other way," said Syed Aziz, who was dismissed cheaply twice, including the first ball in the Super Over.
Aqeel Wahid (4-39) and Virandeep (3-23) grabbed a combined seven wickets as Hong Kong folded for 209.
Kahan Challu led Hong Kong with 62 not out off 59 balls, while Anshuman Rath (44) provided crucial support at the top of the order.
Last-man Hassan Khan added a fighting 24 to push Hong Kong past 200.
15fe8f767ae2cb3f: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) decision to stop requiring suspects to wear its orange uniform during remand proceedings is appropriate, but the policy must be applied equally regardless of a person's status, wealth or political position, said a criminologist.

Dr Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid said the key issue was ensuring that investigation and punishment remained distinct, as a person brought before a court for remand was still a suspect and had not been found guilty.

"I think the main point here is that we need to separate investigation from punishment. When someone is brought to court for remand, that person is still a suspect. The court is not deciding guilt at that stage.
"So, in that sense, removing the orange uniform is appropriate. My only concern is that the policy must be clear and applied consistently," she told the New Straits Times.

Haezreena said allowing suspects to appear in civilian clothing could also reinforce the presumption of innocence, particularly given the strong visual association between the orange uniform and criminality.
"The problem with the orange uniform is that once you see someone wearing it, particularly in a photograph, you immediately associate that person with criminality.
"But this person may only be under investigation. So civilian clothing better reflects where they actually are in the criminal justice process."
However, she cautioned that the move could undermine public confidence if there appeared to be different standards for ordinary suspects and prominent individuals.
"In my opinion, the bigger issue is not really the orange uniform. It is whether everybody is treated the same.
"If an ordinary person is brought to court in orange and handcuffs, but a politician or prominent
businessman comes in civilian clothes without restraints, naturally people are going to question this double standard.
"That is where public confidence can be affected," she said.
Haezreena said MACC should introduce a clear written policy governing clothing and the use of restraints, with any differences in treatment based solely on objective considerations.
"If there is a reason for different treatment — security, escape risk or some operational concern — then there should be an objective reason for it.
"Status, wealth or political position should have nothing to do with it," she said.

She said the previous practice of suspects appearing publicly in distinctive orange clothing could also have lasting reputational and psychological consequences, even if they were subsequently not charged or were acquitted.
"Once someone's photograph in that orange uniform is everywhere, that image stays with them even if they are eventually not charged or are acquitted.

"From a criminological perspective, there is also labelling theory. Once society starts seeing you as a criminal, that label can follow you into your work, family and social life even if you are never convicted," she said.
Haezreena said the change could also affect media coverage of corruption cases, as images of suspects in orange uniforms could sometimes overshadow the substance of court proceedings.
"Civilian clothing may reduce that visual impression of guilt and hopefully shift the attention back to the investigation and the court proceedings," she said.
On the use of handcuffs, Haezreena said restraints should neither be imposed automatically on every arrested person nor waived simply because a suspect was prominent.
She said factors such as the risk of escape, violence, previous resistance and potential danger to the suspect or others should instead determine whether restraints were necessary.
"I don't think security and dignity are incompatible. MACC obviously has to maintain custody and ensure that someone doesn't escape or pose a danger," she said.

f479601a9b23c317: JAKARTA: Thick smog has blanketed parts of Indonesia as the vast archipelago for weeks battles to contain fires that have burned large swathes of Borneo and Sumatra.
The hazardous smoke has led to an increase in respiratory problems, forced schools to close, and has been drifting to neighbouring countries including – Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
Here's what to know:
WHERE ARE THE FIRES?
Most of the fires are concentrated on Borneo island, home to vast tropical jungle that Indonesia shares with Brunei and Malaysia, as well as Sumatra.
So far this year, nearly 300,000 hectares of land have burned in Indonesia, according to an independent estimate from the Nusantara Atlas portal.

Indonesia saw an uptick in carbon emissions since late July, and by the end of last month the levels were comparable to previous El Nino years of 2015 and 2019, Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) senior scientist Mark Parrington told AFP.

"We're seeing already now... really extreme fire emissions comparable to those previous strong El Nino years, and also the extent of the smoke and the haze and the air quality impacts," Parrington said.
Fires in the archipelago have released more than 23 million metric tons of carbon emissions between August 28 and September 3, according to CAMS' Fire Emission Watch portal.
It was higher than 20.7 million metric tons of emissions from fires over the same period in 2015, which was a strong El Nino year.
WHAT CAUSES THE FIRES?

Analysts said that the El Nino weather phenomenon, which the United Nations said this week could turn out to be the strongest in four decades, has contributed to creating drier conditions in Indonesia and made it easier for fires to spread.
But slash-and-burn land-clearing practices also contributed to the damage, said David Gaveau, founder of the Nusantara Atlas.
"El Nino does not ignite fires. It creates the dry conditions that allow human-started fires to escape and become very large," he told AFP.
The fires are difficult to extinguish because many occurred on peatlands, a wetland ecosystem with layers of partially decomposed organic materials that become flammable when dry.
Between January and August this year, more than 210,000 hotspots were detected in peatland areas across the country, according to NGO Pantau Gambut.
"Peat is a naturally wet ecosystem and stores large amounts of organic material. When peat is drained, this organic material is converted into fuel," Pantau Gambut spokesman Wahyu Perdana said.
WHAT IS THE IMPACT?
More than five million people across Borneo and Sumatra are directly exposed to the health risks from haze, deputy health minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono said last month.
Over 1.4 million students were attending classes remotely, with many schools closed due to worsening air quality, an education ministry official said this week.
In Malaysia, soaring pollution levels prompted the government on Friday to declare an emergency in a region of the Sarawak state in Borneo, with nearly 650 schools closed next week.

In the Philippines, air quality was slowly returning to normal after a week of reaching "very unhealthy" and "severely unhealthy" PM 2.5 levels that saw officials shutter schools in cities and provinces citing the drifting haze.
The haze also drove air quality in Singapore's central region to an "unhealthy" level on Friday, the country's National Environment Agency data showed.

327bc3242555347c: KUALA NERUS, Sept 5 — An estimated 230 million metric tonnes of plastic waste are projected to pollute Malaysia’s terrestrial and aquatic environments by 2040, the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) has revealed.

Deputy secretary-general (Environmental Sustainability) Datuk Nor Yahati Awang pointed out that approximately 23 million tonnes of this plastic waste are discharged into waterways annually, representing a significant threat to marine ecosystems.

In response, she said NRES has formulated a range of strategies and initiatives to enhance marine waste management nationwide, including the development of a uniform monitoring framework through coastal clean-up programmes.
“These efforts include beach clean-ups, systematic data collection, and monitoring. Reliable data not only facilitates evidence-based policy formulation.

“It also fulfils our international obligations under SDG 14: Life Below Water,” she said during the closing ceremony of the 2026 National Citizen Science Programme: Monitoring and Cleanup of Marine Plastic Waste at Tanjung Gelam Beach here today.
Her address was delivered by NRES deputy secretary of Natural Resource Management Division, Azrina Mohd Said.
Also present was Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) deputy vice-chancellor (Research and Innovation) Prof Dr Muhammad Ikhwanuddin Abdullah.

Nor Yahati said this approach is also recommended by The Coordinating Body on the Seas of East Asia (COBSEA), which emphasises that beach cleanup activities should be integrated with systematic scientific monitoring, uniform waste classification, quality data collection and trend analysis over time.
She stressed that prevention and reduction efforts are vital to ensure marine ecosystems, resources, and biodiversity remain protected and resilient for future generations.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Ikhwanuddin said 165 kilogrammes of waste were collected in less than two hours by over 100 participants during today’s cleanup.

He said the joint programme involving UMT, NRES and the Geng Plastik Ija association focused on collecting and sorting marine debris such as plastics, packaging materials and fishing gear, which have the potential to impact coastal ecosystems.

The data gathered, he added, will help researchers identify the types, volume and distribution of waste along the coastline, serving as a valuable resource to support future studies, monitoring efforts and environmental management planning.

“In addition to the cleanup, participants comprising students, volunteers, and local community members were also educated on marine waste classification, the importance of reducing plastic use, and the role of communities in protecting coastal areas.
“Kampung Tanjung Gelam was chosen for today’s programme due to its significance as a recreational area and coastal ecosystem that requires ongoing monitoring and care,” he said. — Bernama
67a982af8acf38ab: KUALA LUMPUR: A government backbencher believes that it is better for the government to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) if it is more effective than the Sales and Services Tax (SST).
Kepong member of Parliament Lim Lip Eng made the suggestion after taking into account views that the SST should be combined with the GST to ensure a more effective taxation system.
Lim, who is also the Kuala Lumpur DAP secretary, said the government should not create a complicated hybrid tax system merely to avoid using the GST label.
"An effective taxation policy should not depend on the name given to the system. Instead, it should be designed based on how effectively it can be implemented.
"The government should be prepared to consider a well-designed GST with stronger safeguards, faster refund processes and targeted assistance for low-income groups.
"Bring back the GST with proper implementation if the tax system is more effective," he said in a statement today.
Last month, the government was reported to be open to conducting a study on the need to combine the SST with the GST to improve the country's taxation system and make it more progressive.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was quoted as saying that the government would retain the SST as the foundation, but would not rule out adopting certain GST features deemed suitable to create a better taxation system.

Lim also urged the government to demonstrate that it could achieve the RM59.6 billion tax revenue target through the SST this year before formulating a hybrid taxation system combining the SST and GST.

He said the government should provide details on the total amount of tax refunded to businesses against the RM59.6 billion tax revenue target for this year, including how quickly the refunds were processed.

"The government should also provide details on the amount collected after refunds, as well as the sectors still facing issues of double taxation and the additional costs businesses have to bear for compliance.
"These details are not minor matters. Instead, they will determine whether the implementation of a new system will be easier, fairer and more effective than the SST," he said.
96934e98cf21b976: KUALA LUMPUR: Team Flash roamer Zul Hisham "Xorn" Noor has expressed his disappointment after being dropped from Malaysia's Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) squad despite helping the team qualify for the main event.

The 26-year-old was part of the original six-man squad alongside Ealtond "Loleal" Rayner, Aqif Haikal "Zqeef" Azman, Ammar Asyraf "Martzy" Rahman, Muhammad Nazhan "Chibi" Mohd Nor and Muhammad Razif "Sizkaa" Sazali.
The squad competed at a qualifier in Singapore in June.
Malaysia did just enough to finish fifth among eight teams with a 3-4 record, securing the last of five Southeast Asian berths for the main event in Japan.

Originally named as a substitute, Xorn was drafted into the line-up for the crucial tie against Indonesia and helped inspire Malaysia to a 2-1 victory following opening defeats to the Philippines and Myanmar.
Wins over Singapore and Laos put Malaysia on the brink of qualification, but their inconsistency resurfaced in a shock 2-1 defeat by Vietnam in their final match.
However, the one game Malaysia took off Vietnam proved enough for them to edge to the final qualifying spot.
Earlier this week, Malaysia's new-look MLBB squad were leaked on social media.

The leaked line-up features Selangor Red Giants trio Haqqullah "Sekys" Ahmad Shahrul Zaman, Hazziq Danish "Stormie" Rizwan and Qayyum Ariffin "Yums" Suhairi, alongside Bigetron MY's Danial "CikuGais" Fuad and Sizkaa.
Sizkaa is the only player retained from the original qualifying squad.
Xorn revealed that he and the other affected players learnt they had been replaced through a message in a WhatsApp group rather than during a face-to-face meeting.
"There was no face-to-face meeting. They (Malaysia Esports Federation) said there had been a meeting, and then someone was asked to inform the players through the WhatsApp group," said Xorn.
"It was disappointing because playing at the Asian Games was my dream. To be suddenly replaced like that left me frustrated."
Xorn acknowledged that the original squad's performance in Singapore had not been convincing despite securing qualification and believed the selectors wanted a line-up with stronger medal prospects.
However, he questioned why the initial squad had been selected if the members could be replaced after completing their qualifying mission.
"If this had been decided before everything happened, I could have accepted it," he said.
"But after we had already gone through it, for that reasoning to suddenly emerge was something I could not accept."
Despite his disappointment, Xorn backed the replacement players and urged them to deliver for Malaysia in Aichi-Nagoya.
"I wish all of you the best because this is about our country," he said.
"You are considered the best players for now, and I hope you can give everything for Malaysia and bring home a medal."

875fdf64a90bb6c5: SAN FRANCISCO, Sept 5 — The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said Friday that it has opened an investigation into Tesla’s certification that its new Cybercab meets all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS), reported Xinhua.

The probe, formally designated as an Audit Query, was opened on Sept 3 and covers an estimated 1,000 Cybercab vehicles, according to an NHTSA investigation document. It will examine the process and technical data Tesla relied upon when certifying the Cybercab, as well as related issues.

Tesla began commercial deployment of a small number of Cybercab vehicles in Austin, Texas, on Thursday and notified the agency that it had certified the vehicles as compliant with all applicable FMVSS. Tesla also told the NHTSA that it plans to gradually expand commercial deployment of the Cybercab to include additional vehicles and locations.
The vehicles lack permanently attached conventional manual controls, such as a brake pedal, gas pedal, steering wheel and mirrors, according to the NHTSA.
The agency said the inquiry will examine, among other issues, the extent to which Tesla’s certification depended on determinations that certain FMVSS are inapplicable to the Cybercab.

In the United States, the NHTSA establishes vehicle performance requirements, while automakers must certify that their vehicles meet applicable standards before entering the US market, subject to agency oversight to confirm compliance. The NHTSA said it conducts investigations when certified vehicles appear not to adhere to those requirements.

NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison said the agency fully supports the safe development and deployment of automated vehicles but stressed that as the federal regulator it must ensure that applicable laws are followed.

The NHTSA said it is in the process of overhauling federal vehicle safety standards and has begun work on eight rulemakings over the last year, including standards relating to brake pedals, windshield wipers, lighting and rearview mirrors.
Existing standards will remain in force until that work is completed, the agency said. — Bernama-Xinhua
3764d9bc9a1faab1: SEOUL, Sept 5 — IU is finally ready to return to the music scene. Her label, EDAM Entertainment, announced Friday that the singer will unveil a new digital single next Thursday — a release that effectively ends a year‑long pause brought on by a stubborn ear condition that disrupted her schedule.

The agency shared a brief teaser clip on her social platforms but kept everything else under wraps, including the song’s name and concept. The drop will be her first new track since Bye, Summer, which arrived in September last year.

The upcoming single is expected to mark the beginning of her gradual return to full promotional activity as she continues recovering.
81c6ca73b392acb9: PETALING JAYA: Pemuda PKR membidas Timbalan Presiden PAS Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man kerana mempertahankan Umno berhubung kata dua supaya parti itu memilih sama ada untuk kekal dalam kerajaan perpaduan atau beralih menyokong Perikatan Nasional (PN).

"Sejak bila PAS dilantik menjadi jurucakap Umno. Atau sekarang PAS merasakan mereka lebih besar daripada Umno sehingga boleh bercakap bagi pihak Umno," kata Ketua Penerangannya Danish Hairudin dalam satu kenyataan.

Danish berkata hanya beberapa minggu lalu, Tuan Ibrahim mengingatkan PAS dan Umno bahawa tidak sepatutnya wujud konsep 'abang besar' atau 'adik kecil' dalam rundingan mereka, sebaliknya semua pihak perlu dilayan secara sama rata.
"Hari ini lain pula ceritanya. Bila mahu kerjasama dengan Umno, katanya jangan ada 'abang besar'.

Pada 16 Ogos lalu, Tuan Ibrahim berkata sebarang formula kerjasama antara PN dan Barisan Nasional (BN) bagi PRN Melaka perlu berasaskan kesamarataan dan tidak hanya tertumpu kepada pembahagian kerusi negeri.
“Kita tidak seharusnya menganggap sesiapa sebagai abang besar atau adik kecil,” katanya.

Semalam, Tuan Ibrahim berkata PKR tidak sepatutnya memberi kata dua kepada Umno sama ada mahu kekal dalam kerajaan perpaduan atau beralih menyokong PN, kerana PKR sendiri bergantung kepada kekuatan Umno.
Beliau berkata PKR perlu menyedari kedudukan serta jumlah kerusi Parlimen dan DUN dimilikinya berbanding Umno, sebelum mengeluarkan kenyataan berbentuk amaran kepada rakan dalam kerajaan.

Beliau mengulas desakan Naib Ketua Pemuda PKR Nabil Halimi supaya Umno menyuarakan pendirian dengan jelas sama ada mahu terus bersama kerajaan perpaduan atau beralih menyokong PN selepas Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi menyarankan PRU16 wajar diadakan lebih awal.
