3fa7bd620b8082ba: BOGOTA: A guerrilla drone attack on a military garrison in Colombia killed at least two soldiers and wounded five others on Friday, authorities said.
President Abelardo de la Espriella, who has pledged to get tough on crime, blamed the country's largest active armed group, the National Liberation Army (ELN), for the attack.
"To the ELN I say with absolute clarity: for every police officer or soldier you kill, I will bring down on you the full weight and legitimate force of the State," he said on X.
The attack took place in Ocana, in the northeastern Catatumbo region, where De la Espriella's government is currently conducting military operations against guerrillas.
A military source in the region told AFP that at least 20 drones loaded with explosives were used.
Colombia is the world's largest cocaine producer and is grappling with its worst violence in a decade.
Since taking office, De la Espriella has stepped up bombings and ground operations against armed groups.
Colombia has also joined the Shield of the Americas, US president Donald Trump's anti-cartel alliance of Latin American countries including Argentina, Ecuador and El Salvador.
De la Espriella is set to receive US state secretary Marco Rubio in the Caribbean city of Barranquilla next week.
88cff929b898225a: WASHINGTON, Sept 5 —The United States (US) will not grant birthright citizenship to children of foreign government employees born in the US if neither parent is a US citizens, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said in a document, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.

“DHS is also clarifying that a child of a foreign government employee is not subject to the jurisdiction of the US for purposes of birthright citizenship unless at least one parent of the child is a US citizen,” the document published on Friday said.
DHS added that a child of a foreign government employee is eligible for permanent residence in the US.
The US considers foreign diplomats as foreign government employees. —Bernama-Sputnik/Ria Novosti
98a5ad58550bea00: KUANTAN: Kafe Secangkir in Sungai Karang Darat here, which was run by the late Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, closed its doors yesterday and will be handed over to a new tenant.
Her brother, Muhammad Hafiz Rifqi, 33, said the decision on the new tenant would be up to the premises' owner.

c385cf4a9b360ca0: KUALA LUMPUR: Six areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Serian registering the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 287 as of 1pm today.
No areas recorded hazardous air quality.

Department of Environment deputy director-general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the six areas were Serian (287), Kuching (267), Samarahan (242), Sri Aman (251), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201).
She said 25 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, while 26 recorded moderate readings and 11 recorded good air quality.
"Among the areas recording unhealthy readings were several locations in Johor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, Sabah, Sarawak and Selangor.
"In Sarawak, Limbang recorded an API reading of 160, Miri (182), Mukah (188), Kapit (151), Sibu (172) and Sarikei (179)," she said in a statement.
She said the readings were recorded amid continuing dry weather conditions across parts of the southern Asean region.
"The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) detected 139 hotspots in Kalimantan, 138 in Sumatra and 16 in Malaysia as of Sept 4.
"Of the Malaysian hotspots, five were detected in Sabah, nine in Sarawak and two in Terengganu.
"The ASMC also reported moderate to dense haze moving northeastwards from Kalimantan towards parts of Sarawak, Sabah and Brunei."

Moderate to dense smoke was also observed over North and East Kalimantan, as well as central and southern Sumatra, while moderate haze was reported over Singapore, southern Peninsular Malaysia and eastern Java.

cee5d8019c861713: MELAKA: The Melaka government will study a proposal to make the state one of the earliest in Malaysia to set a basic salary of between RM2,500 and RM2,800 before submitting its recommendation to the Federal Government.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal would be assessed from all angles before being submitted to the Federal Government.

"This is to ensure that our young people have better incomes to build their future in the state," he told reporters after attending the 2026 Melaka Youth Town Hall session at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh, here today.
He said the state government would also create opportunities for women who had left their careers due to various factors, particularly through new projects being developed in the state.

We will look at similar opportunities at the Inland Port in Alor Gajah. We will see if there are suitable jobs for women to move forward," he said.

ff18c53a382ec604: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Manchester United’s enduring global appeal was on full display at the Malaysia Airlines Pavilion at the Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (Matta) Fair 2026 today, with more than 500 fans turning up to meet club legends Park Ji-sung, Wes Brown and Edwin van der Sar.
The event not only drew supporters from across Malaysia but also fans who travelled from overseas, a testament to the English Premier League giants’ worldwide following.

Among them was avid Red Devils memorabilia collector Adam Schwereb, 52, from Sydney, who flew into Malaysia to attend the event and meet the Manchester United legends, an opportunity he described as “too good to be missed”.

“I flew in last Wednesday to come to Matta Fair. It’s always a good opportunity, coming in from down south to catch up with the boys. And it’s Manchester United; we travel the world for it,” he told Bernama on the sidelines of the fair here.

Schwereb, who has attended matches at Old Trafford on several occasions, said events such as this provided supporters who could not travel to England with a rare opportunity to meet their footballing heroes in person.
The lifelong supporter said the initiative was particularly meaningful for younger fans who could now meet players who had played a key role in Manchester United’s decorated history.
He also revealed that the trip would add two prized pieces to his personal Manchester United collection, with items from Park and Van der Sar becoming part of his museum in Sydney.
Young Vietnamese fan Nguyen Danh Truong, 12, was among the foreign fans at the event, travelling from Ho Chi Minh City to Malaysia with his father Nguyen Van Tai.
Truong, who is spending three days in Malaysia, said the meet-and-greet session was the sole reason his father planned the trip.

Meanwhile, Bryan Foong, chief executive officer of Airline Business at Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), the parent company of Malaysia Airlines, said the strong response from supporters reflected the strength of Manchester United’s fan base globally and the value of the airline’s partnership with the club.
“It’s very popular. A lot of people come. It also helps us to create the business and the buzz around Malaysia Airlines as well,” he said.

Foong said the airline’s three-year partnership with Manchester United, which began in 2023, had so far been particularly effective in boosting the national carrier’s visibility and market presence, given the club’s extensive fan base across markets it served.
“The fan base for Manchester United is huge, right? And for us, they’re important and spread out across the world.

“Wherever we are, in terms of where we fly to, like Australia, Southeast Asia, India and even to the United Kingdom, they’re very well received and the Manchester United fans are very loyal. So it’s a good partnership for us,” he said. — Bernama
e942afb5cf8c7979: KOTA BHARU: Presiden PAS Hadi Awang mendakwa parti itu pernah ditawarkan pihak asing untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan.
Katanya, perkara itu berlaku ketika lawatan bekas presiden Amerika Syarikat (AS), Barack Obama ke Malaysia pada 2014, apabila beberapa pemimpin PAS dijemput bertemu di Kedutaan AS.
Beliau berkata, Takiyuddin Hassan dan Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar yang merupakan setiausaha politiknya ketika itu pergi ke kedutaan berkenaan bagi mengadakan pertemuan.
“Saya nak cerita, masa Obama datang melawat ke Malaysia, masa itu kita masih lagi dalam gabungan, parti-parti, kita diajak berjumpa di Kedutaan Amerika.

“Kita atur Takiyuddin dengan Samsuri, setiausaha politik saya masa itu. Dia (pihak AS) nak ajak bincang, sanggup nak jatuh kerajaan, nak ambil alih kerajaan Amerika sanggup tolong,” Hadi berkata demikian ketika menceritakan pengalaman itu semasa ucapan penggulungan sempena Muktamar Tahunan PAS Ke-72 di Pusat Tarbiah Islamiah Kelantan (Putik).
Hadi berkata, dua pemimpin PAS berkenaan bagaimanapun tidak terpengaruh dengan tawaran tersebut dan kekal dengan pendirian parti untuk menolaknya.
“Alhamdulillah dua-dua orang kita ini istiqamah, sebab tak nak terpengaruh,” katanya,
Katanya, selepas pertemuan terbabit duta AS meminta bertemu dengannya dan beliau memenuhi permintaan itu bersama Mustafa Ali.
“Duta Amerika minta nak jumpa saya, saya pun tak apalah. Pergi dengan Mustafa Ali...kita berjumpa. Duta Amerika berjumpa, dia tanya apa? Dia tanya siapa PAS cadang jadi perdana menteri?
“Saya kata, siapa Amerika setuju? Tergamam dia, itu jawapan daripada saya. Saya cerita kepada (Dr) Mahathir (Mohamad), Mahathir kata bagus,” katanya.
Dalam pada itu, Takiyuddin mengesahkan perkara tersebut, sambil menegaskan pihaknya menolak campur tangan asing berkait politik negara.

"Wakil daripada kedutaan tanya, adakah PAS merancang menjatuhkan kerajaan Barisan Nasional (BN) pada masa itu? Jadi, kami tak tak bagi apa-apa keputusanlah kerana kita tidak mengharapkan 'interference' daripada negara luar.
"Sebab politik negara kita, negara kitalah, tak boleh campur tangan luar. Kalau parti lain nak campur tangan luar nak menjatuhkan itu ikut merekalah, kami tidak, kami tidak," katanya.
1cfebe14338490f6: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Sarawak has seen a slight drop in tourist arrivals amid the current haze, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
He said the decline was expected to continue until the haze situation improved.

“There’s a little bit of drop in the number of tourist arrivals lately. I foresee this thing will continue on until after the haze is over,” he told a press conference after chairing the Mesyuarat Jawatankuasa Induk dan Sidang Media bersempena dengan Sambutan Perayaan Hari Malaysia Peringkat Kebangsaan Tahun 2026 at a hotel here today.
Abdul Karim said tourists planning to visit Sarawak might change their travel plans due to the haze.
“If I’m a tourist, if I plan to come to Sarawak at this time or to Kuching, I will change my plan if I am from outside,” he said.
He added that the haze was also affecting several forthcoming events, including the Borderland Music Festival, which will take place at the Sarawak Cultural Village on September 11 and 12.
“I’m quite worried myself, but there’s nothing much we can do. We’ll just hope and pray that the haze problem will go down,” he said.
Abdul Karim also advised organisers of outdoor events to monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) and follow guidance from the State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC). — The Borneo Post
8b5dbf095469f7b0: PETALING JAYA: PKR Youth information chief Danish Hairudin has hit out at PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man for defending Umno over its ultimatum for the party to either remain in the unity government or switch its support to Perikatan Nasional.
“Since when was PAS appointed as Umno’s spokesperson? Or does PAS now feel that it is bigger than Umno and can speak on Umno’s behalf?” Danish said in a statement.

He pointed out that just a few weeks ago, Tuan Ibrahim had reminded PAS and Umno during their negotiations that there should be no concept of a “big brother” or “little brother”, and that all parties should be treated as equals.
“Today, the story is different. When it comes to working with Umno, he says there should be no ‘big brother’. But when it comes to attacking PKR, suddenly Umno becomes the ‘big brother’.
“Does PAS’s politics follow principles, or does it follow the seasons?” he said.

On Aug 16, Tuan Ibrahim said any formula for cooperation between PN and Barisan Nasional for the Melaka state polls should be based on equality and should not focus solely on the allocation of state seats.
“We should not regard anyone as the big brother or little brother,” he was quoted as saying.

Yesterday, Tuan Ibrahim said PKR should not issue an ultimatum to Umno over whether it wants to remain in the unity government or switch its support to PN, as the party itself relies on Umno’s strength.
He said PKR should be mindful of its position and the number of parliamentary and state seats it holds compared with Umno before issuing warning-like statements to its partner in government.
He was commenting on a call by PKR Youth deputy chief Nabil Halimi for Umno to either fully commit to the Madani government or quit its posts in favour of PN.
Nabil issued the ultimatum after Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi suggested that the 16th general election be held earlier.
c3713287775497a4: SINGAPORE, Sept 5 — Singaporeans recruited into a long-running investment scheme in China were promised cheap luxury living and a share of Nanning’s economic boom, but some found themselves closely watched and pressured to recruit friends and relatives.

One Singaporean public servant, identified only as Alice, told The Straits Times she was taken on a five-day trip to Nanning in Guangxi back in March after a friend pitched it as an investment opportunity.
She said she was not allowed to explore the city alone, with someone accompanying her everywhere and even following her to the toilet.
During a city tour, she was told: “We cannot get out of the car at all.”

Alice said she was also made to attend mandatory sales sessions in a condominium unit fitted with CCTV cameras, where recruiters promoted the scheme as a way for Singaporeans to “ride the China wave”.
Potential investors were told they could recoup their money by recruiting others, with each new participant said to be worth about S$10,000 (RM31,900).
Participants were expected to pay between S$26,000 and S$50,000 (RM83,000 and RM159,600), although recruiters were vague about what the money was actually being invested in.
Alice said she eventually paid S$70 (RM223) as a “promise fee” after becoming frightened by what she described as a “cult-like” environment, fearing she would not be allowed to leave if she refused.
While earlier news reports referred to the case as suspected pyramid scheme activity, The Straits Times describes the operation as a Ponzi scheme linked to the 1040 Sunshine Project.
A Ponzi scheme typically uses money from newer participants to pay earlier ones, while a pyramid scheme relies primarily on recruiting new participants to generate returns.

Other Singaporeans interviewed by the newspaper described similar recruitment trips dating back to 2014, with promises that Nanning would become the “next Shenzhen” and that developments there would attract major tourism and investment.
The scheme has also ensnared people from Malaysia, Indonesia, Taiwan and China, according to the report.
The accounts emerged after Singapore authorities announced on Thursday that 52 Singaporeans had been detained in Guangxi over suspected involvement in pyramid scheme activities.
Singapore’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has urged citizens to exercise caution over schemes involving recruitment, large upfront payments or promises of unusually high returns.
64d08d5c12acb040: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Kuala Lumpur has arrested an owner of a consulting, management and business company on suspicion of soliciting and accepting bribes of about RM30,000 in return for obtaining grants and loans under the Bumiputera entrepreneur financial financing scheme for two companies related to armaments and defence.
According to sources, the woman, in her 60s, was arrested at about 6.45pm on Thursday around Kuala Lumpur.

“Initial investigations found that the suspect committed the act in March 2025 and is suspected of soliciting and accepting bribes amounting to about RM30,000 from an owner of a company related to armaments and defence,” he said.

According to sources, a seven-day remand order until Sept 10 against the woman was issued by Magistrate Aliaa Anwar after an application was made by the MACC at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court yesterday morning.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib when contacted confirmed the arrest and the case is being investigated under Section 16(a) (A) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama
136d20b4717e440b: KATHMANDU: Inspired by the "miracle" rescue of two hydropower workers, Nepal's emergency response teams were digging with new vigour Saturday through piles of debris as the death toll from the flooding disaster crossed 1,200.

The rescued pair were among hundreds of hydropower workers who went missing since a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a vast glacial and rock collapse on Aug 26.
So far, 1,294 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the disaster agency, with 5,053 people missing.
In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing. That takes the overall death toll to 1,325 people, with 5,584 missing.
"We have been working since morning on search and rescue operations," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP on Saturday.
Searches continued at the Trishuli 3A tunnel where the two men were rescued on Friday, as well as multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects destroyed by the floods.
"Work is also underway at the tunnels," Basnet said. "We don't have an update yet, but the work goes on."
The government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels.
Rescuers called it a "miracle" after the two men, caked in mud, were pulled out alive after being trapped for nine days.
They were taken to hospital and are said to be in a stable condition.
Experts from India, China, Australia and South Korea have been aiding Nepali rescuers in their search of survivors inside blocked tunnels.
With morgues overflowing, some 1,030 bodies hade been buried in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification by family members, Nepal Police said Saturday.
Prime minister Balendra Shah promised to provide "safe and comfortable accommodation" for thousands of people displaced by the disaster and currently living in temporary relief camps.
"We know that staying there (camps) is not easy for you," he said in an emotional post on social media late Friday.
"(But) we will once again create an environment where you can dream about and build your future," he said.
cbddfb0ed6731d9e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — A total of six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at very unhealthy levels as of 1pm today with Serian recording the highest reading of 287.

Deputy Director-General (Development) of the Department of Environment (DOE) Azuri Azizah Saedon said five other areas in the state that recorded very unhealthy readings were Kuching (267), Sri Aman (251), Samarahan (242), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201).

She said 25 areas recorded API readings at unhealthy levels involving Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak and Selangor, in addition to 26 areas recording moderate air quality status and 11 areas at good levels.
Azuri Azizah said the situation occurred amid persistent dry weather conditions in parts of the Southern Asean Region.

She said based on the report from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) yesterday, 139 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, Sumatra (138) and Malaysia (16), of which nine were in Sarawak, Sabah (five) and Terengganu (two).
“ASMC also reported that moderate to thick haze was observed moving northeast from Kalimantan to several areas in Sarawak, Sabah and Brunei.

“Moderate to thick smoke plumes were also observed in North Kalimantan and East Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra, while moderate haze was observed in Singapore, the southern part of the Peninsula and eastern Java,” he said in a statement today.

In this regard, she said the DOE continued to enhance monitoring and patrols in risky areas including forests, peatlands, landfills, agricultural and plantation areas and industrial areas that could potentially be the source of open burning.

Azuri Azizah said any source of open burning or pollution identified would be investigated and enforcement action would be taken strictly in accordance with the provisions of the law and the jurisdiction of the DOE.

The public is requested to immediately report any fire or open burning incidents to the Fire and Rescue Department via 999 or the DOE toll-free line 1-800-88-2727 to enable immediate action to be taken.
The latest API reading can be consulted through DOE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) at apims.doe.gov.my website or the MyJAS application. — Bernama
5214e1048f680b70: TEHRAN: Iranian media on Saturday reported several explosions near the country's major oil hub of Kharg Island in the Gulf, days after renewed fighting broke out with the US.
Fars news agency said blasts were heard by its correspondent but that there was no smoke visible, while the SNN news agency claimed "an Iranian tanker was targeted by the US" near the island.
There was no immediate comment from US or Iranian officials.
Fighting between the foes resumed last Sunday with US attacks on Iran as their war passed its six-month mark.
The American strikes prompted retaliatory attacks by Tehran on US targets in the Middle East.
Iran said Thursday that its armed forces had hit US military bases in Kuwait and the UAE, vowing to avenge civilian deaths at a wedding that it blamed on Washington.
The two sides also remain vying for control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz, with Iran blocking the passage of ships as Washington maintains a counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
65aca0ece4125e6f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Hani Othman, who has been in Nepal for eight days to follow the developments in the search for her missing Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) officer husband, today joined a mission to distribute humanitarian aid to disaster victims in the country, while hoping to find any clues as to her husband.

Hani, who is currently on her way from Nuwakot to Betrawati with the local non-governmental organisations (NGO) Samundra Nepal NGO and Himalayan Leaders, said that the area they are heading to is not the last location where her husband’s vehicle was detected, but she still hopes that the journey will yield clues.
“The area of my husband’s last point is further up. It’s difficult to access. But Nuwakot is also a disaster-prone area, just located further down.
“I will distribute aid to the victims here. Let’s see, who knows, we might find some clues,” she said when contacted by Bernama.
Hani said that some of the aid items were collected earlier in Kathmandu, while the rest were donated by local NGOs.

Meanwhile, through a social media post, Hani shared that yesterday she managed to distribute aid to disaster victims around Kathmandu, including those who were recently rescued in Timure, and also met the wife of her husband’s team vehicle driver.

She said the contributions from Malaysians were channelled on behalf of her husband, Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, and eight other members of his expedition team, including Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) deputy director of the Fire and Rescue Operations Division Mohd Sani Harul.
“As long as I have known them, they are all good people. They are also generous and like to help others. May Allah ease all their search endeavours and protect them all no matter where they are.
“Set aside religious and ethnic differences for now, let’s pray for the best for all of them,” she said.
So far, Hani has not received news of any new developments regarding the fate of her husband who was reported missing in the flood tragedy in Rasuwa, Nepal on August 26.
Two days after the incident, Hani flew to Kathmandu on her own initiative to get the latest updates on the search and rescue efforts for her husband.

Mohd Fakhrul, 44, was reported missing after the four-wheel drive vehicle his group was in during an expedition to Everest Base Camp (EBC) was believed to have been affected by floods while in a valley in Rasuwa.

A total of 55 Malaysians have been reported as still unreachable following the disaster that occurred on August 26, while 77 others who were found safe in Tibet and Nepal have been brought to Kathmandu to undergo processing before returning to Malaysia.
Anadolu Agency reported that the death toll from the disaster has risen to 1,220, while 4,762 people, including 844 foreigners, are still missing. — Bernama
de0373631a71814b: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia should amend its statutory rape law to protect teenagers in genuine consensual relationships from being prosecuted as sex offenders, a senior lawyer says.

Presenting his paper on “Decriminalising Adolescent Consensual Sex” at a law conference organised by the Selangor Bar Committee today, A Srimurugan said the law should distinguish between sexual exploitation and consensual relationships involving adolescents close in age.
Srimurugan said Section 375(g) of the Penal Code currently treats sexual intercourse with a girl below 16 as rape, regardless of consent.
This could result in a teenage boy being prosecuted for rape even where both parties were minors and the relationship was consensual.
“The rigid legal framework under Section 375(g) of the Penal Code fails to distinguish between exploitative acts and consensual adolescent behaviour,” he said.
Srimurugan said the problem arose particularly when parents discovered such relationships and lodged police reports against the teenage boys.
The law would then treat the girl as a victim and the boy as the offender, potentially exposing him to prosecution under the Penal Code and the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.

He proposed introducing a “Romeo and Juliet” or close-in-age exception, which would prevent criminal prosecution where adolescents engage in consensual sexual activity and there is no coercion, manipulation or force.
Under his proposed amendment, a male below 18 would not be guilty of rape for consensual sex with a person below 16, provided the relationship was voluntary.
The exception, however, would not apply where the male held a position of trust, power or authority over the younger person.
Srimurugan said such an approach would allow the law to protect children from predators while avoiding disproportionate punishment for adolescents involved in consensual relationships.
He stressed that decriminalising consensual sexual activity between adolescents would not encourage teenage sex.
He also proposed replacing criminal punishment with counselling and rehabilitation for both teenagers.
“A criminal conviction for rape can devastate a teen's life,” he said, pointing to possible consequences for education, scholarships, career prospects, and social functioning.
0ecd5acf73cb1f17: SEREMBAN, Sept 5 — All DNA samples from the next-of-kin of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal have been obtained, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said the samples would be sent to Nepal for the authorities there to conduct DNA matching, a process expected to take some time given the large number of victims involved.
Mohamad said Malaysia was also prepared to send experts from the Department of Chemistry to assist the Nepalese authorities with the DNA matching process, if required.

“Many other countries will also be sending their experts to assist Nepal in identifying DNA matches for the victims, which will help expedite the process,” he told reporters after attending the Pinggiran Senawang Independence Carnival here today.
Meanwhile, he said the Nepalese government had been providing excellent cooperation to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu in obtaining the latest information on Malaysians affected by the disaster.

Mohamad said the ministry received daily updates from the Chargé d’Affaires of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu on the search operation and the situation on the ground, while the next-of-kin were also contacted regularly whenever there were new developments.

He said Nepal had limited the entry of foreign search and rescue (SAR) teams to avoid having too many teams on the ground, which could make it more difficult for the local authorities to coordinate the operation.

This morning, 11 officers and personnel from Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) departed for Nepal to assist in SAR operations in areas affected by floods and landslides. The mission is expected to last 10 days.

A total of 55 Malaysians were reported still uncontactable following the disaster on Aug 26, while some of the 77 individuals located safe in Tibet and Nepal have since returned safely to Malaysia. The remainder are expected to return on flights arranged by their respective travel agents.

In another development, Mohamad said he would meet Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in the capital on Monday to discuss efforts to enhance security in southern Thailand, as well as bilateral issues between the two countries.
He said Malaysia had been given the honour by Thailand to serve as a facilitator in negotiations with the parties concerned to help bring about peace in the region.
He added that the meeting would also discuss the best approach to ensure that efforts to promote security and peace in southern Thailand could be effectively implemented.
Mohamad said peace in the region would benefit both countries, particularly by boosting Malaysia-Thailand border trade, which is of significant value.
He also advised Malaysians planning to visit Thailand to remain vigilant and always prioritise their safety. — Bernama
2abe30e3fbaf3afd: SINGAPORE, Sept 5 — A Chinese national has been slapped with a record S$560,000 (RM1.74 million) fine for masterminding a scheme to smuggle nearly 30,000 bottles of duty-unpaid beer into Singapore.
Han Xiaoyang, 47, pled guilty yesterday to seven charges of fraudulently evading duty, Singapore-based news outlet CNA reported, citing information from the Customs Department.
“Investigations revealed that Han had conceived and orchestrated a scheme to import duty-unpaid beer from China into Singapore through false declarations,” Customs was quoted as saying.
But Han did not pay the fine and as such, will instead serve 164 days in jail in default.
The seven charges centred on his evasion of roughly S$60,127 (RM187,000) in duty on 28,236 bottles of beer.
According to the news report, judges also took into account 15 further charges, comprising four counts of duty evasion and 11 counts of evading Goods and Services Tax.
Han’s accomplice, 29-year-old countryman Tong Baobao, was sentenced separately in May for his role as general manager of Wan Changya International (WCI), the company used to run the operation.
Tong pled guilty to three counts of fraudulent duty evasion involving about S$39,517 (RM123,000) and was fined S$322,000 (RM1 million).
He too failed to pay and served 80 days in jail instead.
The scheme came apart on Nov 19 last year, when Customs officers raided an industrial unit along Tagore Lane and caught two workers unloading a liquor shipment.
That single consignment held 4,044 bottles of unpaid beer, and follow-up searches turned up a further 31,016 bottles stashed elsewhere.
“To carry out the scheme locally, he used a Singapore-incorporated company and directed Tong to act on his instructions,” Customs said.
Investigators found that Han told Tong in August last year of his plan to import duty-unpaid beer from China for storage and resale in Singapore, boosting profits by dodging tax.
Tong was instructed to get a China-based freight forwarder to misdeclare the beer as non-dutiable goods such as food items or industrial machinery.
Han bought the beer in China and shipped it to WCI in Singapore under those false declarations, after which Tong arranged for it to be warehoused and delivered to local buyers.
Singapore law provides a fine up to 20 times the evaded duty and a maximum jail term of one year for anyone convicted of dealing in duty-unpaid liquor.
28ea9a9d2078b6b0: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The historic Chew Jetty here was unaffected by a fire that broke out about 20 metres away and destroyed five business premises early this morning, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the state government was ready to provide assistance to the owners of the five business premises, including support for rebuilding efforts.
“This involves government land. I believe the owners of the affected premises are either tenants or Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) holders.

“Should the owners decide to rebuild the affected premises, the state government will assist in the process,” he told reporters after visiting the fire site today, accompanied by Tanjung MP Lim Hui Ying, who is also Deputy Minister of Women, Family and Community Development.

Five business premises near the Chew Jetty area here, including a car workshop, a welding shop and a timber factory, were destroyed in a fire that broke out at 1.08am today, with no casualties reported.

Chow said the Penang Fire and Rescue Department, assisted by the Volunteer Fire Brigade, had brought the fire under control, while efforts to remove the timber stacks continued after traces of the fire were detected in the wooden structures.
Situated along George Town’s iconic waterfront, Chew Jetty is part of the Unesco World Heritage Site and has been home to generations of the Chinese community since the 19th century. — Bernama
e919f6d4e7aef9b7: KATHMANDU: Angka korban akibat kejadian gelongsoran lumpur di Nepal melepasi 1,300, menurut polis Nepal, lapor Xinhua.
Menurut maklumat terkini dikeluarkan, sebanyak 1,344 mayat ditemukan setakat 5 pagi waktu tempatan Sabtu.

Polis memaklumkan 4,898 masih tidak dapat dihubungi setakat pagi Sabtu, manakala 8,631 orang berjaya diselamatkan setakat ini ketika agensi keselamatan meneruskan operasi mencari dan menyelamat di kawasan terjejas akibat gelongsoran lumpur.

Pihak berkuasa turut mempergiat usaha mengenal pasti identiti mayat menerusi ujian DNA. Sampel DNA telah diambil daripada 1,260 mangsa terkorban dan 972 ahli keluarga mangsa, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan sampel dikumpulkan sebanyak 2,232.
81a77f99034e39f9: SINGAPORE, Sept 5 — Singapore’s updated influenza vaccine for the Northern Hemisphere season will arrive about two weeks later than usual, as an industry-wide delay in vaccine production comes amid rising flu cases and demand for jabs.

The Ministry of Health (MOH) and Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA) said yesterday that supplies of the 2026-2027 Northern Hemisphere vaccine are expected to reach public and private healthcare providers in early to mid-October, Singapore-based news outlet CNA reported today.
The vaccine is typically available in Singapore by the end of September, ahead of the Northern Hemisphere flu season, which generally runs from October to March.
MOH and CDA said the delay was due to pharmaceutical companies taking longer to develop the latest vaccines, whose composition includes changes recommended by the World Health Organisation (WHO).
The delay comes as Singapore sees an increase in influenza cases, although the CDA said there was no indication that infections were more severe than usual.
Meanwhile, some clinics are already facing shortages of the current Southern Hemisphere vaccine as demand for flu jabs increases.
CNA found that three of 11 clinics contacted had run out of the Southern Hemisphere vaccine, while another said it had little stock left.

Healthway Medical, Raffles Medical and Parkway Shenton also reported increased demand for influenza vaccinations, with Healthway saying demand had risen steadily following the National Day long weekend.

The updated Northern Hemisphere vaccine is preferred for people at higher risk of severe influenza, including those aged 65 and above, children aged six months to under five years and people with underlying medical conditions, MOH and CDA said.

Those in these groups who have not received the 2026 Southern Hemisphere vaccine can consider getting it for interim protection, before receiving the Northern Hemisphere vaccine when it becomes available.
A minimum interval of eight weeks should be observed between the two doses, the authorities said.

For travellers heading to the US, Europe or Japan between December and February, Raffles Medical executive medical director Dr Chng Shih Kiat said the timing of vaccination would depend on their destination, travel date and health status.
He advised travellers to receive any influenza vaccine at least two weeks before their trip.
bd18c33b51d4356b: JAKARTA: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by encroaching wildfires to their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday.

The vast Southeast Asian archipelago has for weeks been fighting wildfires blanketing parts of Borneo and Sumatra with smog, with haze also contributing to air pollution in Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
The orangutan pair had been under observation since July after being spotted in a plantation area near a forest in West Kalimantan, a local natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.

However, authorities decided to evacuate them to a rescue centre managed by the wildlife foundation Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) on Thursday as the fire spread near their habitat.
Their health is being closely monitored by veterinarians, but a preliminary check found no burn injuries on the two great apes.

"Exposure to smoke over a period of time... can affect the orangutan's respiratory system, especially when smoke concentrations in the habitat are very high," YIARI's veterinarian Komara, who like many Indonesians, uses only one name, said in a statement.
"Both individuals will continue to be monitored while they are at the rescue and rehabilitation centre," it said.

"The latest rescue means nine orangutans have been evacuated because of threats from wildfires in less than a month in the Ketapang district of West Kalimantan province," YIARI operational director Argitoe Ranting said.
"This shows that fires not only destroy forests but also deprive animals of shelter and food," Argitoe said.
Most animals "do not have many options" to relocate as their habitat burns, he added.

One orangutan died after being rescued last week, with a necropsy result pointing to smoke exposure as the cause of death, the West Kalimantan natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.

7f0321918d75f79a: KUALA LUMPUR: Enam kawasan Sarawak mencatatkan indeks pencemar udara (IPU) sangat tidak sihat setakat 1 tengah hari tadi dengan Serian merekodkan bacaan tertinggi, 287.

Timbalan Ketua Pengarah (Pembangunan) Jabatan Alam Sekitar (JAS) Azuri Azizah Saedon, berkata lima lagi kawasan di negeri itu merekodkan bacaan sangat tidak sihat ialah Kuching (267), Sri Aman (251), Samarahan (242), Samalaju (202), dan Bintulu (201).

Beliau berkata, 25 kawasan mencatatkan bacaan IPU pada tahap tidak sihat melibatkan Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak, dan Selangor, selain 26 kawasan mencatatkan status kualiti udara sederhana dan 11 kawasan pada tahap baik.
Azuri Azizah berkata, keadaan itu berlaku dalam persekitaran cuaca kering yang berterusan di sebahagian Rantau Selatan Asean.

Beliau berkata, berdasarkan laporan Pusat Meteorologi Khusus Asean (ASMC) semalam, 139 titik panas dikesan di Kalimantan, Sumatera (138), dan Malaysia (16), iaitu sembilan di Sarawak, Sabah (lima), dan Terengganu (dua).
“ASMC turut melaporkan jerebu sederhana hingga tebal diperhatikan bergerak ke arah timur laut dari Kalimantan ke beberapa kawasan di Sarawak, Sabah, dan Brunei.

“Kepulan asap sederhana hingga tebal turut diperhatikan di Kalimantan Utara dan Kalimantan Timur serta bahagian tengah dan selatan Sumatera, manakala jerebu sederhana di Singapura, bahagian selatan Semenanjung dan bahagian timur Jawa,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Azuri Azizah berkata, sebarang sumber pembakaran terbuka atau pencemaran yang dikenal pasti akan disiasat dan tindakan penguatkuasaan akan diambil dengan tegas mengikut peruntukan undang-undang serta bidang kuasa JAS.

Orang ramai diminta segera melaporkan sebarang kejadian kebakaran atau pembakaran terbuka kepada Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia melalui talian 999 atau talian bebas tol JAS 1-800-88-2727 bagi membolehkan tindakan segera diambil.
8fcb6edb27fae061: KOTA BHARU: PAS no longer wants to give up winnable seats to other parties in upcoming elections.
PAS election director Sanusi Nor said that the party would identify the constituencies in which it has the potential to win.

“We will determine which seats are suitable and can be won by PAS. We should no longer give up those seats to anyone,” he said in his winding-up speech at the 72nd PAS muktamar at the Pusat Tarbiah Islamiah Kelantan here today.
Sanusi said PAS should not be in a situation where its members do the groundwork for another party, only for that party to eventually field the candidate.
He said PAS had for too long faced a situation where its strength and support were not fully translated into political control.

“Our people go over and help them, and we’re happy. Then their party grows while ours remains small. They get to field the candidate, while we become their election machinery. That’s madness. Let’s speak frankly,” he said.
He said PAS needed to stop feeling inferior when negotiating with other parties, and reminded members that the party had a long political history and considerable strength.
“PAS has become an ‘elephant’ of a party. Then suddenly a cat comes along with two or three kittens, and PAS gets scared,” he said, without naming any party.
“Don’t follow that cat. They’re only just starting out. They formed their party two days ago, then came and invited us to join them. And we follow them. That’s not right,” he said.
Yesterday, PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang said in his policy speech the party wanted to defend all the state and parliamentary seats it won in previous elections.
He also said the Perikatan Nasional-led states of Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, and Perlis – collectively known as SG4 – should be retained.

Hadi urged the party to set its sights on Pahang, Perak and Selangor and “strengthen PAS and PN’s parliamentary representation” in those states as well as improve its performance in Melaka, which is expected to hold its state election soon.
PAS needs to grow in Johor
Sanusi criticised PAS in Johor for failing to increase its membership despite wanting to contest elections.

“I thought our membership in Johor had grown. But you’re still doing the same amount of work. The election machinery hasn’t grown either. You can’t remain at the same level and expect to get seats,” he said.
He urged PAS to step up efforts to attract new members and establish more branches in the state.

dbcf89bb6cac86e8: After nearly eight years, ESA and JAXA's BepiColombo spacecraft is finally nearing Mercury, as engineers begin the arrival sequence by jettisoning the power module that got it this far. The spacecraft stack separated from the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) on September 3 at around 1400 CEST. After a tense few minutes, controllers confirmed that a preliminary Doppler signal had been detected, indicating that the MTM had separated successfully; by 1552 CEST, it was confirmed that signals had been picked up, indicating that all had gone to plan. The solar panels of the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) were charging the spacecraft's batteries. The next stage involves dropping into orbit around Mercury on November 21. Then the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO) – aka Mio – will be released between December 9 and 10, and a week later MPO will start moving to its final orbit over 480 x 1500 km, with science commencing in April 2027. The arrival is a year later than planned. BepiColombo was supposed to have been orbiting Mercury in December 2025, but problems with the spacecraft's Solar Electric Power (SEP) system meant the trajectory had to be rethought, which extended the spacecraft's cruise. BepiColombo is no stranger to Mercury and has performed six flybys of the planet since 2021. It has also conducted flybys of Venus and Earth following its 2018 launch. The spacecraft is an impressive example of international cooperation. The MPO and MTM are ESA contributions, while the MMO comes from JAXA. ESA also provided the sunshield to protect the MMO during transit. This sunshield will be ejected after the MMO is released. The MPO is the big brother of the BepiColombo partnership, with a main body measuring 2.4 x 2.2 x 1.7 m and a mass of 1,230 kg (including an 85 kg science payload). JAXA's MMO is 1.8 m in diameter and 1.1 m high, and weighs 255 kg (45 kg of which is the science payload). While MPO is 3-axis stabilized and nadir-pointing, MMO will be spin-stabilized at 15 rpm, with its spin axis 90 degrees to the Sun. The goal of the mission is a study of Mercury, "from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind, to the properties of its large iron core and the origin of its magnetic field." The initial mission at Mercury is planned for one Earth year (approximately four Mercury years), although it could be extended by another Earth year. ®

eb565a991b544039: From the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah
For most of my life, I have described myself, rather cheerfully, as a Jill of all trades and master of none.
I have tried my hand at almost everything.

I cook. I sew. I embroider. I design. I garden. I collect. I write. I make things. I take things apart and put them together again. I become fascinated by something, pursue it with enormous enthusiasm, and before long, another curiosity comes knocking at the door.
My hands have never been very good at keeping still, and neither, I suspect, has my mind.
But there was always one thing I never really thought of myself as being.
A scholar.
That belonged to another world: to academics, professors, historians and people who seemed to have known from a very young age exactly what they wanted to study and what they wanted to become.
I was already 64 when I returned seriously to academic life.
At an age when one is perhaps expected to slow down, I did precisely the opposite.
I went back to school.
And somewhere between lectures, books, manuscripts, footnotes and many very late nights, something quite unexpected happened.
I fell in love with learning.
Not with examinations. Not with grades. Not even with the idea of obtaining a degree.
I fell in love with the chase.

One question led to another. One footnote opened another door. A sentence written hundreds of years ago could keep me awake at night. I began looking at old manuscripts and wondering who had held them, who had written them, why certain words had been chosen, and what they might tell us that history had forgotten.
Then I met the Hukum Kanun Pahang.
Or perhaps, more accurately, I met it again.
It had been there all along. But for the first time, I began to see it not merely as an old manuscript belonging to Pahang, but as a voice from another age.
And I began asking questions.
Too many questions, according to some people around me.

One discovery became another. Melaka led me to Pahang. Pahang led me to Sultan Abdul Ghaffar Muhyiddin Shah. The laws led me to the sea. The sea led me to sovereignty. And somewhere along the way, the thesis I thought I was going to write began refusing to become the thesis I had planned.
That was perhaps my first real lesson as a student.
Do not tell history what you want it to say.
Listen to what the evidence is trying to tell you.
So I followed it.

I followed it through manuscripts and histories, through laws and royal genealogies, through ports and rivers, through Melaka and Pahang, sometimes with excitement, sometimes with frustration, and occasionally with tears.
And on July 27, at the age of 65, I submitted my Master’s thesis:
The Hukum Kanun Pahang: A Sovereign Malay-Islamic Constitution.
A few weeks later, I received my examination results.
The average mark from the two examiners was 91%.
My internal examiner recommended the thesis for acceptance without any modifications or amendments in content, while my external examiner required only very minor corrections.
I read the reports.
And then I cried.
I cried, and I screamed.
Not very scholarly behaviour, perhaps, but after months of work, doubt, discovery, late nights and wondering whether I had understood the manuscript correctly, I could not help myself.
I had never expected this.
But it was not only the marks, or even the absence of corrections from one examiner and the very minor corrections from the other, that moved me.
Both examiners believed that the work should go beyond the examination room.

My internal examiner wrote that the thesis demonstrated “originality, coherence, and scholarly adequacy” and was therefore “suitable for publication.” Its strength, he observed, lay in reframing the Hukum Kanun Pahang as a sovereign Malay-Islamic constitution, embedding Sharīʿah principles within adat, and highlighting the balance between royal authority and accountability.
He concluded that these contributions provided “a fresh civilisational lens that enriches Malay legal historiography.”

My external examiner similarly recommended that the findings of the thesis should be disseminated through academic publications and conference presentations, to highlight their importance to Malaysia’s inherited constitutional and legal identity.
Those words meant a great deal to me.

I had begun this journey simply wanting to understand an old manuscript that had captured my imagination. I never imagined that at the end of it, my examiners would tell me that what I had discovered deserved to travel beyond my thesis and into the wider academic world.
And then I laughed.
Because after spending most of my life calling myself a Jill of all trades and master of none, at 66 years old I had finally managed to become—
a Master of one.
But perhaps that is not really what this story is about.
It is not about 91%.
It is not even about a Master’s degree.
It is about discovering, rather late in life, that curiosity has no retirement age.

We are very fond of putting ages upon things. There is an age to study, an age to marry, an age to raise children, an age to build a career and, apparently, an age when we should begin quietly withdrawing from new adventures.
I am beginning to think that is nonsense.
Some flowers bloom in spring.
Others take their time.

Perhaps being a late bloomer does not mean that one has arrived late. Perhaps all those earlier years, the cooking, sewing, creating, reading, raising children, serving, listening, observing, succeeding, failing, beginning again, were not detours at all.
Perhaps they were preparation.
Because when I finally entered that library and opened those manuscripts, I did not arrive there only as a student.
I brought a lifetime with me.
And perhaps that was my advantage.
I had spent 66 years learning before I realised that I was a learner.
I had spent a lifetime searching before I discovered what I was searching for.
I had spent years calling myself a Jill of all trades and master of none.
Then, very late in the garden, a little flower appeared.
And I discovered that I had been growing all along.
I am a late bloomer.
And I think I rather like blooming late.
But above all, I know that all knowledge comes from Allah. Whatever I have learned, whatever I have discovered, and whatever little contribution I may have made are only by His permission and grace.
Alhamdulillah.

I thank Allah for giving me the opportunity, the strength and the curiosity to continue learning at this stage of my life. I pray that whatever knowledge He has entrusted to me may be used well, shared generously and become something of benefit to others.
I have just registered for my PhD.
And somewhere in the fifteenth century, Parameswara is waiting for me.

P/S: My husband insists that I clarify one important point: I met him before I met Hukum Kanun Pahang. So, in the interests of historical accuracy, let the record show that he was my first great discovery.

The Tengku Ampuan of Pahang, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, holds a master’s degree from the International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilisation (ISTAC), International Islamic University Malaysia.

bcd44a93e77f0903: From Moaz Nair

For 69 years since the nation achieved independence, the non-Muslim community has been a significant strategic partner in the construction and development phases of Malaysia’s geopolitical landscape, spanning from the pre-independence era to the postmodern phase. Their roles extend across multiple critical domains that form the foundation of national identity and national stability.

However, contemporary political dynamics are occasionally still marred by the exploitation of religious and racial issues for narrow geopolitical interests, risking damage to the nation's social fabric.

An objective evaluation of the sacrifices made by non-Muslim communities is highly essential to appreciate their role as one of the main pillars in defending, advancing, and uniting the socioeconomic and political landscape of the country.
The struggle for independence

During the struggle for independence, non-Muslims demonstrated high political tolerance to establish a national consensus. Tan Cheng Lock and VT Sambanthan's participation in a delegation to London alongside Tunku Abdul Rahman reflected a unified goal in demanding independence for the Federation of Malaya.
Tan's role as the founder and first president of MCA in 1949 was highly instrumental as a political architect of unity.

When the Chinese community's loyalty was questioned during the Emergency, Tan united and convinced the community to pledge full commitment to the Federation of Malaya, rejecting the influence of communist ideology and the geopolitics of the People's Republic of China.

Substantive negotiations with Umno and a readiness to compromise and drop certain radical demands enabled the formation of the Social Contract. This legal and social instrument granted citizenship rights to non-Malays in exchange for the recognition of the special position of the Malays.
This pattern of cooperation was further reinforced by MIC within the Alliance Party.

The coalition, comprising Umno-MCA-MIC, demanded great political sacrifice to meet the prerequisites for independence set by the British. Post-1957, this legacy of inclusive governance continued through the active involvement of non-Muslim figures in the country’s executive and legislative institutions as ministers, members of Parliament, and senators.
Defence and security

In domestic defence and security, thousands of non-Muslim security personnel, including the indigenous communities from Sabah and Sarawak such as the Iban, Kadazan, and Bidayuh, were directly involved on the front lines to curb the communist insurgency threat.

Figures such as the late Warrant Officer I Temenggong Kanang anak Langkau, recipient of the prestigious Seri Pahlawan Gagah Perkasa (SPG) gallantry award, became the epitome of the national resilience doctrine.

His commitment was proven by his refusal to surrender despite sustaining severe injuries from three gunshot wounds during a battle in Perak, where he continued to lead his team under the revolutionary slogan, "Agi Idup Agi Ngelaban" (As long as I live, I shall fight).

Statistically, during the peak of the communist threat and the Indonesian Confrontation phase, non-Malay communities made up an estimated 60% of the membership of the 1st Reconnaissance Regiment deployed in domestic operations and United Nations peacekeeping missions in the Congo.
Furthermore, between the 1960s and the late 1970s, non-Malay personnel comprised around 30% of the entire armed forces workforce, with higher representation recorded in the navy and air force.
Historical records estimate that more than 500 soldiers and 1,300 police officers lost their lives during the Emergency.

Apart from the physical military aspects, psychological warfare in the country was also pioneered by a non-Muslim intelligence expert, Too Chee Chew. As the head of the psychological warfare section of the Federation of Malaya from 1956 to 1983, he utilised a deep understanding of the Malayan Communist Party's (MCP) doctrines and ideologies to formulate counter-propaganda strategies through leaflets and radio broadcasts, which effectively prompted thousands of communist guerrillas to surrender.

His capacity as the chief adviser to Tunku Abdul Rahman during the Baling Talks (1955) proved critical in analysing Chin Peng's diplomatic manoeuvres, thereby protecting the nation's sovereignty from the implications of an unfavourable agreement. His sacrifice was immense, given that this role made him a prime target for assassination by the enemy throughout nearly three decades of service.
Economic and social development

In terms of economic development and physical capital formation, early-generation labourers and entrepreneurs from the Chinese and Indian communities were primary drivers of Malaya's extractive sector and basic infrastructure. Their involvement in the tin mining and rubber plantation industries positioned Malaya as a leading global commodity producer.

The surplus capital generated from these sectors funded the construction of the country's earliest public amenities, including educational institutions, hospitals, and modern transportation networks like the road and railway systems.

In the modern era, equity ownership and strategic investments from the non-Muslim corporate sector continue to contribute to gross domestic product (GDP) growth and large-scale job creation. According to data from the statistics department, the non-Muslim demographic constitutes around 30% to 35% of the total citizen population driving the domestic market.

These corporate contributions are balanced by structured corporate social responsibility initiatives based on universal welfare. Corporate giants founded by non-Muslim entrepreneurs channel substantial financial contributions annually through charitable foundations – such as the YTL Foundation, Hong Leong Foundation, and Ananda Krishnan/Usaha Tegas — for academic scholarships and post-disaster humanitarian aid regardless of ethnicity or religious belief.

Additionally, human capital in both the public and private professional sectors is heavily supported by the involvement of the non-Muslim community in medicine, law, the judiciary, higher education, as well as technical and civil service corps, ensuring the continuity of the country's bureaucratic operations.
Sports

In the international sports arena, the contributions of non-Muslim athletes serve as instruments of public diplomacy and national integration. World-class sports legends such as Lee Chong Wei (badminton), Nicol David (squash), Pandelela Rinong (diving), R. Arumugam (football), and M Jegathesan (athletics) have demonstrated high commitment to raising the country’s sporting reputation globally.

The majority of Malaysia's early Olympic medals were contributed by non-Muslim athletes, including three silver medals by Chong Wei (2008, 2012, 2016) as well as the historic achievement of Pandelela as the country's first female athlete to win an Olympic medal (bronze in 2012 and silver in 2016).
Diversity

The diversity of art, culture, and heritage brought by the non-Muslim community has enriched Malaysia’s pluralistic identity on the international stage. The integration of traditional dances, musical expressions, traditional attire, architectural designs, and unique local gastronomy not only strengthens the tourism sector but also shapes a dynamic national cultural ecosystem.

Interfaith human connections are also manifested through inclusive social phenomena, such as the case of Chee Hoi Lan, who raised a Muslim foster child in strict compliance with Islamic practices. Such social narratives prove that national integration and the spirit of racial camaraderie are fundamental elements that must be preserved to guarantee geopolitical stability and the long-term prosperity of the nation.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.

Maka kata Yusri, "sudah tentu Wawasan akan bermatian menuntut dan mempertahankan kerusi tersebut kerana kepada Wawasan merekalah pewaris pusaka Bersatu dalam Perikatan Nasional."
"Jika kerusi tersebut dibahagi sama rata, Umno Terengganu berpotensi bertanding sekitar tiga kerusi sahaja dalam PRU16 nanti. Inilah scenario awal yang boleh difahami."
Itu belum lagi kita bercakap mengenai kerusi Parlimen dan DUN negeri-negeri lain.

Dalam pada itu, penganalisis James Chin dari Universiti Tasmania semalam dipetik FMT berkata Umno tampak cuba melemahkan perdana menteri meskipun berikrar menyokong Anwar Ibrahim sehingga tamat penggal Parlimen.

"Mereka mengenakan tekanan kerana tidak mahu hilang momentum (setelah menang PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan bersama PN serta confident menang PRN Melaka kelak). Adakah Anwar akan tunduk? Saya rasa masih awal untuk bercakap mengenainya. Anwar juga sedang mengatur perikatan baharu tanpa Umno," kata Chin.
Chin menjangkakan hubungan PH-BN akan semakin buruk sambil Umno terus berdolak dalik. Saya setuju dan tidak mungkin Anwar dan PH tidak perasan.

Berikutan ucapan Hadi semalam, Umno tertekan. Jika usul wajib berkait kerjasama dengan Umno diterima sebelum muktamar ditangguhkan hari ini, Umno tertekan juga tetapi saya tidak pasti adakah ia relevan memandangkan apa yang diucapkan Hadi yang saya sebut tadi.

Amat menarik apa agaknya reaksi Perhimpunan Agung Umno terhadap perkembangan di muktamar PAS. PAU akan berlangsung minggu depan yakni 9 hingga 12 September. Menarik juga kerana kepimpinan tertinggi PAS diundang ke upacara perasmian. Adakah Hadi akan hadir? Iya, kata Asyraf.

Menutup penulisan ini saya ulang apa yang pernah dinyatakan pada artikel terdahulu iaitu Umno sedang buat apa yang ia tuduh PAS buat dulu sehingga terkuburnya Muafakat Nasional. Apa yang PAS buat waktu itu? Bermain dua kolam, kata Umno. PAS berbaik dengan Umno dan pada masa sama berbaik-baik dengan Bersatu, musuh ketat Umno.
Sekarang Umno berbaik-baik dengan PH di peringkat persekutuan dan berbaik-baik dengan PAS di peringkat negeri sambil menyerang PH. Ertinya Umno main dua kolam.
Bagi saya sudah sudahlah main dua kolam. You can't have your cake and eat it too. Itu kata omputih. Orang Melayu kata simple je: "jangan nak makan kelilinglah".

39168a9833287356: From Ong Tze Chin
The government’s plan to fast-track the e-commerce bill and consider registration requirements for platforms is timely.

E-commerce platforms are not neutral connectors between sellers and consumers; they are complex ecosystems built on heavy investments, extracting rental income from locked-in consumers and dependent businesses.
While platforms appear “free” to users, sellers pay steep costs—search ads, commissions, vouchers, and shipping campaigns—to remain visible.
Through network effects, data concentration, and control over transactions, platforms dictate how businesses access markets and reach consumers.

Their power and decision-making effectively make them private regulators, governing both businesses and consumers. Dependence on algorithmic profiling, automated decisions, and predictive analytics deepens the imbalance of power.
A recent fundamental research grant study by Universiti Malaya’s law faculty identified several major harms in Malaysia’s e-commerce sector:
Market access, data dependency
Platforms set operational rules—visibility rankings, traffic, fees, and data insights.

Meanwhile, businesses build reputation and rankings over time, but this visibility is tied to platform data, which cannot be replicated elsewhere. Non-transferability locks sellers in, strengthening platform dominance and widening the power gap.
Price, advertising pressures

By leveraging data and AI analytics, platforms fuel intense price and advertising competition. This forces businesses into trade-offs between cost efficiency and product quality, undermining long-term consumer welfare.
Predatory pricing

Platforms often sell below cost, subsidising vouchers and shipping to drive weaker competitors out. Exclusive contracts with affiliated businesses further distort competition, as transaction revenues fall below logistics and fulfilment costs.
Self-preferencing

Platforms use internal data to identify successful third-party products, replicate them under private labels, and manipulate search algorithms to favour their own offerings. This sidelines independent sellers.
Algorithmic bias
Search and recommendation systems are coded to favour certain products or brands, undermining neutrality and fairness.
Data asymmetry
Platforms aggregate granular transaction and consumer behaviour data from sellers, using it to optimise proprietary retail strategies, leaving sellers disadvantaged.
Algorithmic repricing
Automated pricing tools trigger margin wars, forcing smaller sellers into unsustainable profit thresholds.
Fee exploitation
Locked-in businesses face rising fees, mandatory ad spending, and high fulfilment costs simply to maintain visibility.
Vertical restraints
Platforms enforce price-parity clauses, mandatory discounts, and algorithmic penalties, stripping sellers of pricing flexibility and eliminating competition.
Exclusive dealing

Platforms restrict sellers to list exclusively on their marketplace (“single-homing”), penalising cross-listing. Though competition law limits exclusivity to two years, platforms’ shorter contracts often auto-renew, cumulatively foreclosing competition and reducing consumer choice.
Tied logistics

Platforms increasingly force sellers to use their own logistics services, sidelining independent delivery companies and raising costs for businesses with existing systems. Consumers lose delivery options, while competition in logistics is destroyed.
Unfair Contracts

“Take-it-or-leave-it” contracts impose restrictive clauses on both businesses and consumers. Price-parity rules prevent sellers from offering cheaper prices elsewhere, while sudden changes in platform terms expose both sides to exploitation. Consumer protection laws are weakened as liability is shifted away from platforms.
Cross-border factory dumping

Certain platforms integrate directly with Chinese manufacturers via proprietary software, dictating production in real time. This model bypasses import taxes through loopholes, flooding markets with cheap, unsafe products. Platforms cannot claim neutrality when they control supply chains, data, and algorithms.
Copying and grooming

Platforms mine seller dashboards to identify successful local products, replicate them through white-label factories, and push replicas to the top of feeds. Local merchants often find their intellectual property registered abroad, undermining expansion efforts.
International precedents

Global regulators are acting against platform abuses. In the US case of Oberdorf v. Amazon (2019), Amazon was held liable as a “seller” for defective third-party products, recognising its active role in sales and distribution.
In Europe, the Digital Services Act (2022) imposed record fines on AliExpress (Euros €550m) and Temu (€200m) for failing to curb illegal and unsafe goods.

Closer to home, Thailand introduced strict platform regulations in 2022, the Philippines enacted the Internet Transactions Act (2023), Vietnam suspended Temu and Shein for registration non-compliance before passing its Law on E-Commerce (2025), and Indonesia banned Temu to protect local industries.
Conclusion
Malaysia’s upcoming e-commerce bill must directly address structural algorithmic, competitive, and consumer harms.
Platforms are not neutral intermediaries but powerful private regulators shaping markets, data flows, and consumer access.
Without robust legal boundaries, Malaysia risks undermining trust in e-commerce, harming consumers, and weakening domestic retail and manufacturing sectors.

That's not something many consumers want at the moment, but the AI biz this week published a set of templates for Claude-based shopping agents and merchant agents in the hope of encouraging more e-commerce businesses to implement automated purchasing. Its blueprint "contains the harnesses, patterns, and guardrails an engineering team needs to get a commerce agent running in days, with reference implementations of a shopping agent and a merchant agent for retail, travel, telecom, and ticketing platforms," the company said. Large retailers and ecommerce platforms, Anthropic observes, are using Claude to build AI agents to simplify online shopping by allowing customers to pose natural language queries to find, compare, and buy items. The buying bit may be wishful thinking: A recent Gartner survey found that while consumers use AI to find products and conduct research, they're not ready to delegate purchasing authority to AI agents. The survey found just 11 percent of consumers are willing to let AI make purchase decisions. A recent Accenture survey [PDF] is a bit more optimistic, noting, "Three in four (74 percent) consumers would let an AI agent handle routine tasks; one in three (32 percent) are ready to hand over purchase decisions; and 9 percent are open to fully autonomous shopping, before the technology is fully operational." Either way, at least AI-assisted product finding and comparison appear to be plausible activities. Anthropic's GitHub repo contains functional shopping and merchant agents that can be built with the Messages API, Agent SDK, or Claude Managed Agents. The biz's shopping agent blueprint comes with ways to connect to product catalogs, online shopping carts, checkout systems, preference databases, and purchase history databases. "A customer can say 'I need a tent, sleeping bag, and stove for a weekend trip with two kids,' and the agent can take it from there," Anthropic suggests, noting that its code supports guardrails "designed to constrain prices and products to actual catalog data, and avoids manipulative upsell patterns." Why might prices need constraint? Well, beyond the possibility of hallucinated pricing, there's considerable concern about how AI agents have the potential to compound the problems with dynamic pricing – where customers are charged different amounts for the same goods. "The rise of agentic AI, where algorithms monitor online behavior to customize costs, will likely exacerbate dynamic pricing," said the Brookings Institution earlier this year. "These agents can assess individual behavior and tailor prices based on a consumer’s shopping and purchasing history." Concerns about AI surveillance pricing were discussed last month at a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing. In prepared remarks, Lindsay Owens, president and CEO of Groundwork Collaborative, a Washington, DC-based advocacy group, noted that already half of those using the Walmart app use "Sparky," the company's AI assistant. Those shoppers spend about 35 percent more than those who don't, Owens said. "These agents have access to swaths of data on customers – what shoppers tell them, what they’ve purchased in the past, and in some cases, what they’ve hovered over with their mouse or even what other websites they’ve visited," she said. "All of that can be used to infer exactly how much they’re willing to pay for a product and set the price tag accordingly." Even if shoppers can be assured of getting a fair deal using AI agents, there's another concern. Monica Eaton, founder and CEO of Chargebacks911, told The Register in an emailed statement that agentic commerce looks likely to create fraud problems for merchants. There isn't yet a framework for merchants to deal with AI purchases that consumers claim they didn't authorize. "Merchants cannot become the insurer of every misunderstanding between a consumer and their AI," she said. Anthropic's templates may prove helpful for AI agent design, but the real challenge isn't technical. It's about trust – consumers have to trust that AI will act in their best interest and merchants have to trust that AI will be accountable. That may take time. ®
